title: fix(post): Tormach states the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

**`tormach.cps` now states the clearance height before a section's first X/Y traverse.** This applies after a tool change, after a G30, and at the program start. An upright section first writes `G0 Z<clearance>`:
- the clearance is the stream's `PARAM ClearancePlane`, else its `RetractPlane` (the hop, #1028);
- it is never below the move's own Z.

A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, once per program: "first X/Y traverse ... with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) ...". Indexed (4th-axis) sections keep their own order: `indexFor` lifts with G53 and turns A, and their X/Y is the turned tip. The microARC tester-kit program shows the clearance landing right after `G0 A0`.

**Why (from a PathPilot Hub run, 770MX sim v2.14.4).** Hub's T4 was 5" long, and the session's G54 Z zero sat about 4.3" below the top of Z travel. After `G43 H4` the tip stood about 0.68" under the part top, and the bare `G0 X.. Y..` crossed the part at that height. The user saw "down, over, up". #1596 re-lifts with `G53 G0 Z0` after `G43`, which covers a low stored G30. The top of travel itself can still be below clearance when the tool is long for the work offset; that is what this PR covers.
- On a setup that can clear, the new `G0 Z` is an ordinary move down to clearance before the traverse.
- On a setup that cannot, the control refuses that block as past its Z limit and the program stops. It no longer rapids through the part.

`assets/posts/AGENTS.md` states the law.

### Goldens regenerated (WRITE_GOLDEN=1); each gains exactly one `G0 Z..` line before its first X/Y traverse, nothing else
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/`: the 13 legacy programs (`contour_disc_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `drill_peck`, `drill_plate`, `face_square_40x40`, `face_square_40x40_stepped`, `pocket_waterline_plate_with_island`, `pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island`, `slot_fullwidth_centerline`, `slot_wide_channel_rows`, `tap_plate`, `trace_plate_with_hole`), plus `index_4face_microarc4`, `probe_bore_centre`, `probe_bore_centre_mm`, `probe_boss_centre`, `probe_corner`, `probe_edge`, `probe_face` and `probe_guard_moves`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/tormach/`: `contour_plate_with_hole`, `drill_peck`.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_tormach.nc`: `G0 Z5` (its ClearancePlane 10 minus OriginZ 5).
- `crates/post/tests/golden/ream/tormach.nc`.
- `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach/`: `arcs`, `drill_retract`, `extreme_coords`, `full_circle`, `full_circle_raw`, `probe`.
- `docs/tester-kits/tormach-microarc-4th/microarc_test_part.nc`.

That is 32 files, 32 added lines. No snapshot PNG was touched.

### Test inputs given the plane a real section carries
- `tests/common/legacy_program.rs` `as_program` now states `PARAM ClearancePlane` from the legacy golden's `START` height.
- These hand-written streams gain `PARAM ClearancePlane`: `tormach_post.rs`, `tormach_program_end.rs`, `tormach_routers.rs`, `tormach_safe_retract.rs`, `tormach_toolchange_lift.rs`, `tormach_fourth_axis.rs`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle.rs` and the post crate's `work_offset_index.rs`.
- `tormach_post::the_first_move_after_a_tool_change_positions_xy_with_z_up` now asserts the new order: a Z-only `G0 Z0.3937` (the 10 mm clearance), then X/Y alone.

## Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/tormach_traverse_clearance.rs`)

| Test | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first` | the `G0 Z` is removed |
| `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated` | the `G0 Z` is removed, or the RetractPlane fallback is removed |
| `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height` | the `G0 Z` is removed, or the max with the move's own Z is removed |
| `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` | the refusal is removed |

All four mutations were checked; each one fails the test(s) above.

## How tested
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post` (all debug suites) before the input and golden updates: 14 targets failed. All of it was the expected fallout listed above. After the updates every one passes.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites, app suites 885 s, 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- **The Hub re-run.** The new `drill_peck` and `contour_plate_with_hole` (inch, 770MX) are in the user's hub-tests folder `1614-770MX/` for that run.
- **The other mill posts.** They have the same pattern and are filed as **#1616** (P1, effort:high, area:post): grblhal and carvera make a bare X/Y traverse; the Fanuc family makes a combined first rapid from the tool-change height.
- The release-lane `--ignored` suites and the UI suites (no UI code touched).

Changelog: The Tormach mill post states the section's clearance Z before its first X/Y traverse after a tool change (and refuses a stream that states no clearance or retract plane), so a tool too long for the work offset stops at the control's Z limit instead of rapiding through the part.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Fixes #1614

title: fix(2d): judge Engrave/Trace as a mark and keep the part under the pocket family, on the operation itself
body:
Fork synced at v0.19.0; branch merged with upstream/main f2b42e3d (#1597 is in it).

Two P1s with one root: a 2D operation at `DepthLaw::None` had no judge of its own, so its verdict rode on the program sim, and the sim refuses a turned stock. Both are fixed with a law the operation carries. `uncovered()` is unchanged (see below).

## #1595 - Engrave and Trace: the mark law
- `DepthLaw::Mark` (`crates/app/src/operation/mark_law.rs`) for both kinds on a finished-part source, whole model or pick. Under the cutter the part's surface may give way by the **mark budget**, `min(Top - Bottom, cutter radius)`, and no more.
- The test is the existing solid law (`verify::solid_hits`) run against the part lowered by the budget. A cutting move that still enters it is a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on that move, and the path carries a note that names the budget.
- It convicts three things: a cut deeper than a mark, a Top typed below the surface, and a wall standing beside the line (a picked pocket floor is traced along the wall's foot).
- The program sim credits the same mark (`stock_sim::credit_marks` in the sim crate, beside #303's `credit_breaks`; the shared walk is now `edge_break::credit_floors`). A column the mark's own cutter swept is judged against `max(that sweep, model top - budget)`. The budget is computed from the operation each time, never read from the cached path, and only an Engrave or Trace on the part declares one.

Readings on the #1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, 6 mm end mill), whole-model source, Top 8:

| cut | before: aligned / turned | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.02 mm, 0.3 mm deep | refused by the sim / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| 3.0 mm deep (the radius) | refused by the sim / posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| 3.1 mm deep | refused by the sim / posts | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| 7 mm deep (the issue's repro) | refused by the sim / **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| Top typed 7 (surface at 8), 0.3 stated | refused by the sim / posts | yes | refused / refused |
| pocket floor picked, 0.3 deep | - | yes | refused / refused |

So before this PR no engraving on a model could post on an aligned stock (0.02 mm included), and any depth posted on a turned one.

## #1603 - the pocket family: the keep law
- `DepthLaw::Keep` (`crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`) for 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset on a whole-model source: the solid law alone, against the source's mesh. It applies where the pocket clears the stock around the part (#12). With no stock set up the model is still the volume to remove, and the law stands down (`GenJob::around_part`).
- On a **stock source** (or a pick off the stock) the same law runs against the setup's parts (`setup_align::parts_facets_in`, the mesh the program sim judges against), carried in the job as `keep_parts`. A setup with no part judges nothing.

Readings on the #12 fixture (30 x 30 x 10 block, 12 x 12 boss to Z20, 10 mm end mill, 50 x 50 x 20 stock), cut to Z5:

| case | before: op gouges, turned stock | now: op gouges | now: aligned / turned |
|---|---|---|---|
| whole model, Area offset +3 (Pocket, Adaptive) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| whole model, extension +5 (Pocket, Adaptive) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| stock source (Pocket, Adaptive; #1554's cut) | 0, **posts** | yes | refused / refused by the op's moves |
| whole model, default controls (Pocket, Adaptive, Offset) | 0, posts | 0 | posts / posts |
| stock source stopping on the part's top | 0, posts | 0 | posts / posts |

## `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs): not changed
Both issues asked whether a None-law op on a model source should stop counting as judged when the sim cannot judge. It was measured against its own test and declined:
- it would refuse every legal whole-model Pocket, Adaptive and Offset on a turned stock (they were at `None`), which is a false refusal;
- it keeps the verdict tied to whether the sim can model the stock;
- it cannot name the move.

With `Mark` and `Keep`, the only 2D kind still at `None` on a model source is the 2D Chamfer (derived depth, credited by #303). The legal rows above post on a turned stock, pinned.

## Existing tests that changed
Three fixtures ran a stock-source pocket straight through a part and asserted a silent verify. Each is a real cut into the part, which #1603 asks to be refused:
- `post_not_judged.rs`, `machine_switch.rs` (the tilted pocket): the part filled the whole stock. The part is now the 10 mm the pocket leaves, so the cut stops on it. The assertions are unchanged.
- `lead_approach.rs` (two tests on the user's stock-source pocket on `Milling-test.step`): they now assert the gouge on the user's part and read the entry laws on the remaining warnings.
- `authored_law_tests.rs`: #1593's audit table is split into `the_2d_chamfer_alone_stays_unjudged_on_the_part`, `the_pocket_family_keeps_a_whole_model_and_sections_a_pick` and `engrave_and_trace_on_the_part_answer_to_the_mark_law`.

No golden and no snapshot changes. `golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens` pass unchanged.

## Pins
`crates/app/tests/engrave_law.rs` (9; generate, then post, on both stocks; Engrave and Trace):
- `a_whole_model_cut_deep_under_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`
- `a_shallow_mark_is_clean_on_the_operation_and_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `the_mark_budget_ends_at_the_cutter_radius_on_both_stocks_alike`
- `a_top_typed_under_the_surface_is_not_a_mark`
- `a_picked_floor_traced_along_its_wall_gouges_the_wall_and_never_posts`
- `a_picked_top_face_marked_shallow_posts_on_both_stocks`
- `a_cut_on_the_stock_is_never_judged_by_the_mark_law`
- `the_program_sim_credits_the_mark_and_nothing_past_it`
- `over_mcp_a_whole_model_engrave_and_trace_are_judged_the_same` (MCP `add_operation`, `verify`)

`crates/app/tests/keep_law.rs` (7; Pocket and Adaptive, both stocks):
- `a_whole_model_area_offset_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_whole_model_extension_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_stock_source_cut_through_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts`
- `a_legal_whole_model_clearing_stays_clean_and_posts_on_both_stocks` (Pocket, Adaptive, Offset)
- `a_stock_source_cut_that_stops_on_the_part_stays_clean_and_posts`
- `a_stock_source_cut_with_no_part_in_the_setup_judges_nothing`
- `over_mcp_the_pocket_family_keeps_the_part_the_same` (MCP `add_operation`, `set_operation_area`, `verify`)

`crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs` (6) and the unit tests in `mark_law_tests.rs` (7) and `authored_law_tests.rs`.

Both fixtures place the box stock centred over the part and assert its bounds.

| mutation (each alone, then reverted) | result |
|---|---|
| M1 Engrave / Trace arm back to `None` | red: 6 (deep, radius, low Top, wall, MCP, law table) |
| M2 budget without the radius cap | red: 5 (deep, radius, MCP, sim credit, budget unit) |
| M3 budget without the stated depth | red: 3 (low Top, sim credit, budget unit) |
| M4 part not lowered (the plain solid law) | red: 6 (shallow, picked top, radius, MCP, 2 units) |
| M5 sim mark credit removed | red: 5 (shallow, picked top, radius, MCP, sim credit) |
| M6 sim floor not held to the budget | red: 2 (`mark_credit`, sim credit) |
| M7 sim credits a stock-source cut | red: 1 (sim credit) |
| M8 pocket-family arm back to `None` | red: 4 (offset, extension, MCP, law table) |
| M9 stock-source parts not collected | red: 2 (stock source, MCP) |
| M10 `Keep` with no stock set up | red: 1 (`tilt.rs` parked pocket) |
| M11 `part_solid` early return disabled | red: 5 (stock never judged x2, 3 law tables) |
| M12 lowered part raised 0.05 (over-conviction) | red: 6 (shallow, picked top, radius, MCP, 2 units) |

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 976cda6c (sim suites 101 s, motion 3 s, app suites 974 s, ui suites 31 s, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean. `golden_cl`: 32 passed. The mutations were run on 086f4010, before the last merge of main.

## Not exercised
- The mark and keep laws under a 3+2 frame with a part to keep. The framed branch feeds the local mesh to the same solid law; `tilt.rs` covers only the no-stock stand-down.
- On an aligned stock, when both judges convict, the post's refusal leads with the program sim's clause (the gate's existing order, as in #1597). The op's own gouges are asserted on the op and over MCP.
- The stock-source keep law tightens by the stock's fidelity excess, not each part's.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets` fails on `tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs:152` (`needless_range_loop`), which this PR does not touch; the sim lib and the new suite are clean.
- `stock_sim.rs` (app) grew 467 to 477 lines and `generate.rs` by about 60; both were over 400 already. The new code is in new files.

## Follow-ups filed
- #1607 (P1): stock-source Engrave, Trace and the typed kinds cut the part with no op finding and post on a turned stock. Probed here for Engrave and Trace (7 mm, 0 findings, posts). #1603's fix covers the pocket family only.
- #1608 (P7): `trochoid_law.rs` places its stock beside the part (a box stock is centred on its place), so its aligned rows judge a quarter of it.
- #1554 stays open for its generate-side behaviour (rough the stock minus the part; the skipped narrow band).

MCP: no new command or tool. The existing `add_operation`, `set_operation_area` and `verify` reach both laws (pinned).

Decision: `docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md` (both issues, the `uncovered()` decision, and the correction to #1593's audit bullet, which holds only with the default area controls).

Changelog: An Engrave or Trace on the finished part is judged as a mark (no deeper under the part's surface than the lesser of Top - Bottom and the cutter radius) and a 2D Pocket, Adaptive or Offset keeps the part under an area offset, extension or stock source: a deeper cut is a blocking gouge on the operation and the post is refused even where the program sim cannot judge; a legal engraving on a model now posts (#1595, #1603).
Effort: max (no escalation; #1603 folded in at the coordinator's request)

Fixes #1595
Fixes #1603

title: fix(post): Tormach lifts Z after each tool change before moving X/Y
body:
## What changed

Every Tormach PathPilot mill tool change posted `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `S.. M3`, then `G0 X.. Y..` with no Z lift between. A bare `G30` leaves Z at the stored G30 height. One stored below the part top (the user's PathPilot Hub sim had machine Z -1.5611, the same cause as #1594) rapids the tool sideways at that height into the part or the vise. M3's review of #1600 raised this to P1.

- `assets/posts/tormach.cps` `startPreamble`: `liftZ()` (`G53 G0 Z0`, or the machine's stated safe Z, #495) right after `G43 H..`. It comes before the spindle start and before the section's first X/Y or A move, including the program's first tool change. The tool-change `G30` stays (PathPilot's convention).
- 4th axis: the new lift comes before `G0 A..`. The index's own lift is kept, so an indexed section has a second, harmless `G53 G0 Z0` just before `G0 A`.
- The issue's other two bare G30s are kept, with the reasons in `docs/decisions/1596-toolchange-lift.md`:
  - **Plasma.** The G30 height is PathPilot plasma's traverse height (rapids carry no Z, and M205 returns to it).
  - **Lathe.** G30 is the X/Z safe spot and there is no "up" to lift to. The lathe's diagonal approach from G30 is a different hazard, filed as #1604 (P3).
- Not stacked: #1600 merged first, and this branch is one commit on current main.

## Pins and mutations

New `crates/app/tests/tormach_toolchange_lift.rs`:

| Pin | Proves |
|---|---|
| `every_tormach_mill_tool_change_lifts_z_before_moving_xy` | Every shipped Tormach mill, both tool changes (the first included): `G43` is followed by `G53 G0 Z0`, the G30 is kept, and there is a lift between each G30 and the next X/Y move. |
| `a_stated_safe_z_is_the_lift_after_the_tool_change` | `safe_retract` 2.0 gives `G53 G0 Z2` after each `G43`. |
| `a_fourth_axis_section_lifts_z_before_the_a_index` | microARC 4: the lift after `G43` comes before `G0 A90`, and A is the first sideways move. |

Mutation check against `tormach.cps`: each mutation was applied, the pins run, and the file restored. All pins were green again after the restore.

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove the lift | 3/3 pins red |
| Hard-code the lift to `Z0` | `a_stated_safe_z…` red |
| Move the lift to the end of the preamble (after the spindle and coolant) | 3/3 red |

`tormach_program_end` (#1600) stayed green under every mutation and on the fix: the program end is unchanged.

Updated tests:
- `tormach_safe_retract::a_stated_safe_z_posts_that_z`: the `G53 G0 Z<stated>` count goes from 3 to 5.
- `probe_spindle_stop` (post crate): a `G53` line is a machine-coordinate retract, not the section's first move. The probe `M5` still comes before any work move.

## Goldens

Regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. The tester-kit `.camproj` rewrite that came with it was reverted (unrelated version/float noise).

- 33 `.nc` files changed: 24 app goldens (tormach + inch/tormach + synth_tormach), 8 post goldens (recorded tormach + ream) and the microARC tester-kit `.nc`.
- `git diff -U0 -- '*.nc'` shows exactly **35 added lines, all `G53 G0 Z0`, and 0 removed**: one per tool change.
- No lathe or plasma goldens changed. No snapshot PNGs were touched.

## Gates (macOS, debug)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: ok. The post suites passed (15 s). The app suites passed: the whole app set, since shared goldens changed (800 s).
- Also run: post `recorded_streams` / `script_tormach_plasma`, and app `recorded_post_streams` / `posting` / `lathe_post_tormach` / `tormach_lathes`. All ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No PathPilot Hub or machine run of the new tool change.
- Windows arms of per-OS readings were not run.

Changelog: Tormach mill posts lift Z straight up (`G53 G0 Z<safe>`) after every tool change, before the first X/Y or A move, so a low stored G30 never carries the tool sideways into the part (posted output changes: one line per tool change) (#1596)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1596

title: fix(circular): rings post as arcs, not 512 fixed chords
body:
## What changed

A Circular ring was a closed polygon of 512 chords at every radius, and the helix entry's fallback ramp ("the helix stands down to a ramp along the first cut") walked that polygon back and forth. One Ø6 hole was 74,131 moves of 0.006 mm.

- **Ring cut = two half-turn arcs** about the authored centre at each level (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`, `ring_walk`). G3 for climb, G2 otherwise, starting at the same +X point the polygon started at, so travel direction and climb are unchanged. The ladder walks them through `run_level_walks`, the same `Seg::Arc` walk Bore and Contour use.
- **Polygon sized by tolerance, not 512.** The ring polygon is still used for planning: descent placement, links and the length of the zig-zag ramp. Its chord count is now the fewest power of two from 8 to 512 whose sagitta is within `ARC_FIT_TOL` (0.01 mm), for example 32 for R1. A power of two divides the 512-gon that the cutter-centre disk certificate is built from, so every ring vertex is still a certificate vertex and descents certify exactly as before.
- **The ring ramp flies helical arcs** (`links::push_zig_ring`). It keeps the same out-and-back legs and the same travelled length, so the ramp angle is unchanged. Each leg is at most two half turns, the same pieces `entry::helix_about` already posts. Only Circular opts in (`Motion::with_ring_zig`). Pocket, Bore, Contour and every other ladder keep `push_zig` byte for byte.
- Entry choice, lead, ramp angle, stepdown, stepover, ring-major sequencing and the verify laws are all unchanged.

## Move counts: the issue's table, before and after

Fixture: a 40 x 40 x 10 plate with a modeled Ø6 through hole, `EM-0400-2FL`, the issue's MCP params (seeded Circular plus its patch), whole-model source. The **before** column is upstream main 7bfb1824 on the same fixture and reproduces the issue's numbers exactly.

| Circular params | before | after | arcs after | warnings before -> after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| repro (helix R1, stepover 0.5) | 74,131 | **417** | 364 | 0 -> 0 |
| `entry: plunge` | 13,416 | **156** | 52 | 0 -> 0 |
| `helix_radius: 0.5` | 13,446 | **186** | 108 | 28 -> 28 (the same XY-crossing warnings the issue reports) |
| `stepover: 1.0` | 26,937 | **159** | 132 | 0 -> 0 |
| `stepover: 2.0` | 26,937 | **159** | 132 | 0 -> 0 |
| `radius: 4.0` | 26,858 | **338** | 208 | gouges -> gouges (12,585 -> 345, fewer moves to flag), post still held |
| `radius: 6.0` | 53,690 | **650** | 416 | gouges -> gouges (37,544 -> 811), post still held |
| `stepdown: 2.0` | 67,989 | **345** | 316 | 0 -> 0 |

The radius 4 and 6 rows cut past the modeled Ø6 wall, so they are gouges both before and after. The arcs are judged, not waved through.

## Pins (each mutation-checked)

- `crates/app/tests/circular_arcs.rs::the_issue_table_posts_arcs_and_verifies_the_same`: every row above has a move ceiling (repro <= 500), at least two arcs per ring-level, the same gouge verdict (in-hole rows clean, radius 4 and 6 still gouges).
- `crates/motion/tests/circular_arcs.rs`:
  - `the_issue_hole_posts_a_few_hundred_moves_not_tens_of_thousands`: the repro is under 500 moves with plunge, helix and ramp entries.
  - `each_ring_level_is_two_half_turn_arcs_about_the_centre`: exactly 52 arcs (2 rings x 13 levels x 2). Each has centre = authored centre, endpoints on R1 or R0.5, a diametric half turn, is planar, has `ccw == climb` (both senses tested), and the first one starts at the polygon's old start.
  - `the_ramp_rides_the_ring_as_helical_arcs`: every ramp move is a falling helical arc about the centre on the ring, out and back legs pair up, at most 12 per ring-level.
- `circular.rs` unit test `ring_chords_are_sized_by_the_tolerance`: the sagitta is within `ARC_FIT_TOL`, the count is the fewest power of two that does it, it divides 512, R1 gives 32, and NaN falls back to 512.

Mutations, each red, then restored and green:
- Old `circular.rs` (512 chords, no arcs): all 3 motion pins red. The app pin is red with "74131 moves over 500".
- `with_ring_zig()` dropped (ramp back to chords): the ramp pin and the move-count pin are red.
- First half arc's `ccw` flipped: the direction pin is red.
- `ring_chords` forced to 512: the tolerance unit test is red.
- `ring_chords` compared against 20 x tol: the tolerance unit test is red.

title: feat(2d): trochoidal method for 2D Adaptive, confined to its region
body:
## What changed

2D Adaptive gets a **Method** choice (maintainer's decision of 2026-11-13, "Adaptive op only"):

- **Spiral** (default): the HSM plan the kind always ran. Same bytes, same stamp; no existing golden moved.
- **Trochoidal**: trochoid loops inside the operation's region (its selection and boundary settings).

This is the 2D Adaptive slice of #1509. 2D Pocket is not touched (#1517). 3D Adaptive and the rest are filed as sub-issues (below).

### The trochoidal method (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch.rs`)

- The cutter-centre area is the region eroded by the tool radius plus the stock to leave (the pocket's own law).
- The lane is that area's medial line (`adaptive::medial`), straightened. The loop band is the least clearance along it, so every cutter-centre point is inside the area by construction.
- The loops, the measured-engagement step ladder and the lifted returns are the Trochoidal slot's planner (`trochoid_slot`, #220). The forward step is at most optimal load x D; the limit is 90 degrees of contact, measured on the dexel stock.
- The finished path is then checked move by move against the area (`confined`). A point outside refuses the whole operation by name, with its place and a ghost.
- A band wider than the tool gets an opened bore (`trochoid_bore.rs`): helix at half the tool radius, then a two-centre semicircle spiral out to the band. A helix of the band's radius leaves a post at the lane's start when the band is wider than the tool. The stand-alone slot keeps its plain bore byte for byte (its own post is #1589).

Sources: Otkur & Lazoglu 2007 and Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009 (trochoidal milling); Blum 1967 and Held 1991 (medial line); Douglas & Peucker 1973 (straightening). No vendor material.

### Refused by name

| Case | Refusal |
|---|---|
| Empty region | `nothing to machine: empty pocket region` |
| Region narrower than the tool | `the region is narrower than the 6.000 mm tool ...` |
| Too narrow to loop in | `the region is <w> mm wide where the loops would run, too narrow for a 6.000 mm tool to loop in (it needs more than 6.260 mm)` |
| Ring round an island | `the region closes round an island ... use the Spiral method` |
| No single medial line (L, T, island pocket) | `the area is no single channel ... use the Spiral method` |
| One lane would leave over 25 % out of reach | `loops along its medial line would leave <n> % of the region standing (at most 25 %)` |
| A loop outside the region | `a loop at (x, y) would leave the region - nothing is cut` |
| Drop past the helix turn cap | `the bore helix would need more than <cap> turns ... (half the tool radius)` |
| Zero / oversized optimal load, zero stepdown | the Adaptive doors (`PocketParams::validate`) |

Under 25 % the unreached area (the corners of a rectangular pocket) is said in the notes in mm2 and per cent.

### Laws

- **Everything is a command**: the Method is an `EditOperationParams` edit (undo / redo tested).
- **MCP**: `edit_operation` / `add_operation` take `"method": "spiral" | "trochoidal"` through the parameter DTO; an unknown word is refused. No new tool was needed.
- **Project file**: `adaptive2_d.method`; absent (every older file) reads as `spiral`. Additive, the format version does not move.
- **Stamp**: the method byte is written only for Trochoidal, so every Spiral operation keeps its stamp.
- **UI**: a Method combo on the Passes tab of 2D Adaptive (not on 2D Offset); structural test only, no snapshot PNG.
- **Decisions**: `docs/decisions/1509-adaptive-trochoid-method.md`. The stand-alone Trochoidal slot operation is kept as the confined slot #1503 made it; nothing is migrated (#1590 asks the maintainer to confirm).
- **Code shape**: new files 32 to 278 lines; `trochoid_slot.rs` went from 405 to 388 lines (its bore moved to `trochoid_bore.rs`); `mill2d_page.rs` stays at 400. No new crate dependency. No `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` outside tests.

## Readings

34 x 16 pocket face, 6 mm end mill, default optimal load (14.6 % of D), two levels:

- 20 loops of radius 5.039 mm a level at a 0.859 mm step; 86.0 degrees measured (limit 90.0).
- No slotting; no feed crosses another (`crossed_pairs`).
- Cutter centre within 0.002 mm of the eroded face.
- 49.7 mm2 (9 %) of the region out of the loops' reach (its corners), said in the notes.
- App level, through the commands: no warning blocks the post, `verification_report` has no problem (the stock sim finds no gouge), Fanuc post writes.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_tests.rs` (12 tests): inside the region and under the limit; the opened bore leaves no post (and the plain bore does); each refusal by name; retract returns without lift room.
- `crates/app/tests/adaptive_trochoid.rs` (5 tests): picked pocket face generates, verifies, posts and matches `tests/golden/adaptive2d_trochoidal_pocket_face.cl`; stamp; too-narrow face refused and nothing posts; undo / redo; older file reads as Spiral; MCP sets the method, refuses an unknown word, generates and verifies.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/adaptive_method.rs` (2 tests): the Method row and its combo value; none on 2D Offset.

Mutation check (each line deleted or neutralised, its test run, then restored): 10 of 10 killed.

| Mutation | Killed by |
|---|---|
| empty-region refusal removed | `an_empty_region_is_nothing_to_machine` |
| narrower-than-tool refusal removed | `a_region_narrower_than_the_tool_is_refused_by_name` |
| too-narrow-to-loop refusal removed | `a_region_too_narrow_to_loop_in_is_refused_by_name_with_the_numbers` |
| ring refusal replaced by "use the closed line" | `a_ring_round_an_island_is_refused_by_name` |
| rest limit 25 % raised out of reach | `a_lane_that_would_leave_most_of_the_region_standing_is_refused_by_name` |
| `validate()` call removed | `a_zero_or_oversized_load_is_refused_by_name_never_looped_forever` |
| path check `confined` neutralised | `a_loop_outside_the_region_is_refused_by_the_check_on_the_path` |
| opened bore switched off | `the_opened_bore_leaves_no_post_at_the_lane_start` |
| stamp byte for Trochoidal removed | `the_trochoidal_method_stays_in_the_picked_face_posts_clean_and_matches_its_golden` |
| `#[serde(default)]` on `method` removed | `a_new_2d_adaptive_is_spiral_and_an_older_file_reads_as_spiral` |

The first version of the stamp test (status goes Stale after an edit) survived its mutation: an edit makes the operation Stale whatever the digest says. The test now compares `current_stamp` for the two methods directly.

Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head 9b79a44b - green, 3 steps, 0 failed (motion suites 417 s, app suites 1929 s, ui suites 55 s; 40.1 min wall). Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion, camcraft-app and camcraft-ui, all targets: clean.

## Not exercised

- No NC (G-code) golden for the new method: the test asserts the post writes, the CL is pinned.
- No GUI run by hand and no machine run. The Method combo is asserted structurally only.
- Curved channels: the lane follows a bent medial line through the slot planner's chain layout, and the path check and the crossing law judge the result, but no test pins a curved region.
- Release-mode heavy lanes were not run (quick tier only).
- The existing `trochoid_slot_small.cl` golden (band narrower than the tool) proves the stand-alone slot's output did not move for that case; a stand-alone slot with a band wider than the tool has no golden, its bore code path is unchanged (`open: false`).

## Sub-issues filed (Part of #1509)

- #1587 - trochoidal method for wide and branching regions (parallel lanes, islands, corner clean-up); P4, effort:max
- #1588 - engagement limit, return and loop width as page and MCP parameters; P7, effort:high
- #1590 - decide the stand-alone Trochoidal slot operation's future; P8
- #1591 - 3D Adaptive: Method choice with a Trochoidal method per level; P4, effort:max
- #1589 - bug found on the way: the stand-alone Trochoidal slot leaves a post at its start when its loop band is wider than the tool; P3

Changelog: 2D Adaptive has a Method choice - Spiral (default, unchanged) or Trochoidal, which clears a channel-like region with loops along its medial line, confined to the region and refused by name where one lane cannot cut it

Effort: max (not escalated)

Refs #1509

body:
Fork synced at v0.19.0; branched from upstream/main 7bfb1824 (after #1585 merged).

## What changed
- `depth_law_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`): `OpParams::TrochoidalSlot` joins the Slot and Circular arm, `Slot | TrochoidalSlot | Circular => authored_law(src)`, still after the `part_solid` early return. An Entity or Selection source naming the finished part is `DepthLaw::Section`; a Stock source (or a pick off the setup's stock) still cuts unjudged.
- #1513's `slot_fit::refuse_unfit_slot` is unchanged. A picked slot that does not fit its region in XY is still refused at generate. The new law adds the depth check, and on a whole model the walls, which the fit check never read.
- **Root cause:** TrochoidalSlot fell to `_ => DepthLaw::None`, so nothing on the operation judged its hand-typed endpoints and width. `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs) counts any fresh, stamped op as judged, so the post relied on the program sim alone. The sim refuses to judge a turned stock, and it missed the through-wall case even with the stock aligned.
- Doc comments, `authored_law_tests.rs` and `docs/decisions/1593-trochoid-law.md` (decision plus an audit of the other kinds) are updated.

## Other 2D kinds still at `None` on a part-solid source (audit)
Probed on the same fixture, with a whole-model source cut to Z1:
- **Pocket / Adaptive2D / Offset2D, whole model:** left as is. By contract the source is the volume to remove. Every move below the floor stays outside the part (radius 23+ against the 20 mm half-block), and the program sim agrees. Picks were already `Section`.
- **Chamfer2D:** left as is. It enters the part by design, and its depth is derived, not typed.
- **Engrave / Trace:** left at `None` (Section would convict legal engravings). They are **filed as P1 #1595**: cut to Z1 on a whole model, they run 3-7 mm under the model. The aligned program sim refuses that, and with the stock turned it posts.
- **Drill with cross holes:** this is the lathe turret's cross drill, judged by its own laws, not a 2D mill kind.

This table is pinned by `the_kinds_that_enter_or_remove_the_part_by_contract_stay_unjudged`.

title: fix(import): STEP face evaluation cap gets measured headroom; finer pass over a continuous face keeps the coarser mesh
body:
## What changed

#1546's per-face evaluation cap (`FACE_EVAL_CAP`, 25 M) refused healthy STEP models (#1568): `10208.STEP` at the 60 M facet budget was refused on face #1073, which converges at 28.07 M evaluations, and `32050.STEP` used 92 % of the cap at the default budget.

- **Cap rule.** `FACE_EVAL_CAP` is now **150 M**, a fixed constant (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_guard.rs`). That is 5.3x the heaviest healthy face measured (28.07 M), and a runaway face still ends in 10-15 s in release. It does not scale with the facet budget: the budget does not bound one face's evaluations, a low budget must not lower the cap, and a broken face's time must not grow with a user setting. 250 M (the issue's "about 10x") was measured and dropped: 17 s on the fixture and 25 s on sc_logo.step, past the 12-15 s target.
- **Fallback rule.** A *refinement* pass (one after a coarser pass met) that trips the cap on a face **proven continuous** stops refining and keeps the coarser mesh at its own reported chord, the way a pass over the facet budget is dropped. The usual reduced-fidelity note applies. Every other trip still refuses by name: a first-pass trip, or any trip on a face that is not proven.
  - "Proven continuous" (new `step_continuity.rs`) is read from the surface's definition: analytic surfaces; a B-spline with every interior knot multiplicity at most its degree and finite control points; a NURBS that also has every weight finite and positive. Swept surfaces are not proven. **And** that pass must have divided the face only inside the surface's own parameter range.
  - Why that is sound: truck's subdivision ends at any tolerance on a uniformly continuous surface, so a continuous face that trips was only expensive. Its coarser pass is a converged mesh.
  - Why the range clause: without it, sc_logo.step's face #836 (a rational degree-(4,2) corner blend with positive weights) passed the proof. truck had divided it over **u from -2e51 to 1**, a trimming bound gone wild at its collapsed corner, and the import kept a 140-facet mesh at a 3.75 mm chord: the smear. With the clause, it is refused by name again.
  - Why not "closed shell, volume within tolerance": measured with the proof forced true, the #1536 fixture's smeared jump imports as 12 facets at chord 0.125, a **closed box of volume 1.0**. That is exactly what such a check would accept. A STEP file also states no volume to compare against.
- A continuous face refused on its first pass is described as "too dense to divide", not as discontinuous.
- **Review fixes (pullrequestreview-5899510189):**
  - When several faces trip in one pass, the pass is continuous only if **every** tripped face is proven and in range; the refusal names the first tripped face that is not (`Guarded::tripped`). Before, only the first tripped face was read, so a proven face tripping beside a jump face kept the jump's smear.
  - The out-of-range flag is **sticky** for the whole import (`Meter::reset` keeps it): the coarser pass a fallback would keep may be the one that divided outside the range.
  - A NURBS weight below **1e-9 of the net's largest** is not proven (near-pole). Recorded in the decision file.
  - `Kept` carries `eval_capped`; the reduced-fidelity log line then says a larger facet budget will not help. The user-facing refusal text still advises a larger budget, because only the chord is stored: follow-up #1592.
- `step_guard`'s unit tests moved to `step_guard_tests.rs` (400-line law). The cap comment and `docs/decisions/1568-step-cap-headroom.md` carry the measured corpus numbers and correct #1536's "a few million" claim.

## Real files (release `camcraft-cli mcp` `import_model`, this head, macOS; local only, not committed)

| File | Budget | Result | Time | M5's baseline on #1546 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10208.STEP | 60 M | **imports, 14,866,333 facets** (same count as main before #1546) | 204.7 s | refused on face #1073 (158 s); main pre-#1546 173 s |
| 10208.STEP | default | imports, 6,095,267 facets, reduced fidelity 0.016 mm | 39.6 s | 6.1 M facets, 31 s |
| 32050.STEP | default | imports, 4,970,610 facets | 79.5 s | 4.97 M facets, 62 s |
| sc_logo.step | default | refused by name: `face #836 (NURBS surface, face 9 of 62 in shell #3148) ... did not converge within 150000000 evaluations` | 14.9 s | refused in 1.8 s |
| testdata bspline_discontinuous.step | default | refused by name: face #53 | 10.0 s | 1.2 s |
| h5.step / sc_logo_softjaws.step | default | 84 / 2912 facets | <0.1 s | same |

None of the three corpus imports tripped a face (no trip or fallback in the warn log). The corpus timings ran while debug builds and tests were compiling on the same machine, so read them as upper bounds.

## How tested

Pins (each mutation applied, the test seen failing, then reverted):

| Test | Pins | Mutation that fails it |
|---|---|---|
| `step_guard::tests::the_cap_keeps_headroom_over_the_heaviest_measured_healthy_face` | the cap is at least 5x the 28.07 M face | cap back to 25 M |
| `step_guard::tests::a_smooth_face_needing_more_than_the_old_cap_is_divided_not_tripped` (heavy lane, release 8 s) | a smooth egg-crate bicubic needing 39.3 M evaluations divides to the end, untripped | cap back to 25 M |
| `import_step_guard::a_finer_pass_that_runs_out_on_a_smooth_face_keeps_the_coarser_mesh` | dome at a 1000-evaluation cap: imports, coarser chord, volume 1 + 0.2/9 | fallback arm in `refine` returns the refusal |
| `step_refine::tests::a_finer_pass_tripping_on_a_continuous_face_keeps_the_coarser_mesh` | same, at the schedule level, keeping the kept mesh's own tol | same |
| `import_step_guard::a_finer_pass_that_runs_out_on_a_face_that_may_jump_is_refused` | the #1536 fixture's first pass meets and the finer one trips: refused by name | `Trip.continuous` forced true (it then imports the 12-facet smear) |
| `step_refine::tests::a_finer_pass_tripping_on_a_face_that_may_jump_refuses_by_name`, `a_first_pass_trip_refuses_even_on_a_continuous_face` | the refusal paths of the schedule | - |
| `step_guard::tests::a_division_outside_the_surface_range_is_flagged` | a division range like sc_logo's (-2e51) voids the proof; round-off does not | range check removed |
| `step_continuity::tests::*` (4) | knot multiplicity > degree, zero/negative weights and non-finite points are not proven; smooth patches are | - |
| `step_guard::tests::a_proven_and_a_jumping_face_tripping_in_one_pass_refuse_naming_the_jump` (review item 1) | a plane (proven) and the #1536 jump face trip in one refinement pass: not continuous, the jump is named, and `refine` refuses | `tripped()` reports only the first trip |
| `step_guard::tests::an_earlier_pass_outside_the_range_voids_a_later_trip` (item 2) | a pass outside the range, then an in-range pass that trips: not continuous | `reset()` clears `outside` |
| `step_guard::tests::a_trip_on_a_proven_face_divided_outside_its_range_is_not_continuous` (item 3) | a rational degree-(2,2) patch with positive weights, divided over u from -2e51 (sc_logo #836's shape), trips as not continuous; in range it is continuous | `tripped()` ignores `outside` |
| `step_guard::tests::a_non_finite_division_range_is_never_within` | `within` refuses a non-finite range against an unbounded one | `within` finiteness dropped |
| `step_continuity::tests::a_nurbs_with_a_non_finite_coordinate_or_weight_is_not_proven` | NaN x / inf y / NaN z / inf w / every weight inf are not proven | NURBS x/y/z finiteness dropped; NURBS `w.is_finite()` dropped |
| `step_continuity::tests::a_non_finite_knot_is_not_proven` | an infinite knot is not proven | knot finiteness dropped |
| `step_continuity::tests::a_swept_surface_is_not_proven` | an extruded line is not proven | `SweptCurve(_) => true` |
| `step_continuity::tests::a_near_zero_weight_relative_to_the_net_is_not_proven` | weight ratio 1e-12 not proven, 1e-6 proven | weight floor dropped |
| `step_refine::tests::a_finer_pass_tripping_on_a_continuous_face_keeps_the_coarser_mesh` / `a_dropped_pass_keeps_the_tolerance_of_the_mesh_it_kept` (extended) | `eval_capped` set only by the cap fallback | `eval_capped` never set |
| `import_step_guard::a_face_that_never_converges_is_refused_by_name_within_the_budget` | default cap: bounded, named; ~27 s debug, 10 s release | (existing #1536 pin) |
| `a_smooth_bspline_face_still_imports_closed_at_its_volume` and the import suites in the gate | normal imports unchanged | - |

- Review-fix head b518c907: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` **green**, 58 s (app lib 221 + 1 ignored, the suites below unchanged); clippy clean; every new pin mutation-checked (table above, 10/10 killed). Real files re-run at that head: sc_logo.step refused by name (face #836, 14.9 s), 10208.STEP at 60 M 14,866,333 facets (225.6 s, machine loaded), h5.step 84 facets.
- First head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **green**, 46 s (app lib 213 + 1 ignored, bore_facet_sagitta 2, import_step_guard 6, large_models 3 + 1 ignored, model_fidelity 9, step_budget 6, step_chord_units 3, step_fidelity 2, step_nesting 8, stock_export 2).
- `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --lib -- a_smooth_face_needing --ignored`: ok (8 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- M5's whole 75-file corpus was not re-run. Only 10208, 32050, sc_logo, h5 and sc_logo_softjaws were, plus the testdata fixtures through the gate. Those three corpus imports produce the same facet counts as before.
- The continuity proof is conservative. Two cases still refuse when a refinement pass trips: a B-spline with a full-multiplicity interior knot whose two control rows coincide, and any swept surface. No such trip is known.
- Edge-curve divisions remain unmetered (#1545).
- The GUI import path was not run by hand. It goes through the same `parse_with_chord_budget`.

Changelog: STEP import no longer refuses healthy models whose faces need many evaluations (the per-face cap is now 150 M); a finer pass that runs out on a provably continuous face keeps the coarser mesh, and a face that may jump is still refused by name (#1568)

Effort: high (not escalated)

title: fix(contour)!: climb milling runs climb - outside clockwise, inside counter-clockwise with M3
body:
**Breaking (post output):** every 2D Contour and 2D Chamfer posted from an existing project changes direction, and G41/G42 swap under control or wear compensation. A project that set `climb: false` to get climb milling now posts conventional. That is why the title is `fix!`. The release notes must say so.

Branched from upstream `main` d00243a5 (fork synced at v0.19.0).

## What changed

With a right-hand spindle (M3, clockwise seen from +Z), climb milling keeps the material on the **right** of the tool's travel. So an outside profile runs **clockwise**, an inside profile (a hole wall) **counter-clockwise**, and control compensation is **G41**. Conventional is the reverse of all three. Source: Machinery's Handbook ("Milling Practice", climb vs conventional milling) for the direction, and RS-274 / ISO 6983 for G41 (cutter left of the contour along the direction of travel). Every 2D mill op posts M3; only thread milling can ask for M4, and it has its own hand law. Adaptive, Bore and Circular already work this way and also don't read the spindle. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1555-climb-direction.md`.

I found the cause where the issue said: `contour.rs` treated "material on the left" as climb. I checked every user of the direction rule and the climb flag:

| Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `machining2d::contour`: outside/inside ring travel | `climb != inside` walked stored (material left) | `climb == inside` walks stored, via `ring::walked` |
| `contour::air_side`: leads, `lead_fit`, `contour_entry`, `contour_chain` | climb meant air on the right | climb means air on the left |
| `Legal::air_left` (fillets, lead room) | `!climb` | `climb` |
| `contour_comp::side_of` (control and wear compensation) | climb = G42 | climb = **G41**, conventional = G42 |
| `contour_comp_room::arcs` (inside-arc room law) | took the tool side from the contour side, which was only right in 1 of 4 cases | takes it from the travel (climb = left) |
| `arc_leads` (comments only) | | sign words updated; the math follows `air_side` |
| `app::operation::contour_open` (contour on an open boundary) | run order was the chain's lexicographic order, unrelated to the side | run handed on with the material on its right |
| `machining2d::chamfer` + app `Chamfer2D` | climb walked stored order (material left on a boss edge) | new `ChamferParams::inside` (from Side): boss edge CW, bore edge CCW under climb |
| 2D Pocket wall pass (Waterline / Offset rings / Adaptive, `waterscan`, `adaptive/wall`) | already CCW under climb | **unchanged**, pinned. The issue's pocket row did not reproduce on main with any strategy (motion disc and app block-with-hole) |
| Zigzag pocket rows, Face rows, Slot rows | serpentine: half the rows are climb whatever the flag | unchanged (the flag only picks the first row) |
| Trace, open centerline contour run | on the line: material on both sides or none | travel unchanged; a centerline run's lead now leaves to the other side (both sides are air as far as the run knows) |
| Deburr | has no climb parameter | unchanged |

Three changes came out of the flip:
- **Seams stay put** (`ring::walked`). Each ring keeps the seam the old default had: the outside ring's first point, the inside ring's last point (the axis-aligned point on a tessellated bore). Climb and conventional now differ only in direction. Without this, the climb bore started on a 0.7-degree facet: its arc entry became an oblique chord fan and the verify flagged `RapidInStock` (`one_descent`).
- **Keep-down ring-to-ring links** are now also checked against both rings' leads. Under climb, the straight link between two bosses crosses the next boss's lead-out arc (verify `Crossing`). It now lifts at that spot, with a note ("staying down would have crossed passes"), instead of posting a crossing that the gate would block.
- **`cl::PathBuilder::push_arc_in`** no longer splits a vertical arc at a Z extremum that sits at the arc's off-lattice end. That split left a 0.2 um sliver arc on the climb bore's arc entry (`arc_entry::the_arc_entry_changes_only_the_descents`).

## Goldens: direction reversed, same geometry, same seam

Regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`, and only the suites that failed. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- CL: `contour_plate_with_hole`, `contour_plate_with_hole_blended`, `contour_disc_hole`, `contour_tangential_lead`, `contour_start_point`, `contour_bore_arc_entry`. Outside rings now run clockwise and hole rings counter-clockwise; leads mirror to the air side.
- NC (each dialect's copy of those programs: fanuc, carvera, doosan-dnm, grblhal, haas, heidenhain, mazak, sinumerik, tinyg, tormach, plus the inch set of `contour_plate_with_hole`): G2 and G3 swap on the walls and on the arc leads.
- NC compensation: `contour_control_comp` and `contour_wear_comp` (fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik). G42 becomes **G41** (climb outside, M3), and `COMP RIGHT` becomes `COMP LEFT`.
- NC `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form`: its roughing contour round the boss now runs G02 (clockwise).
- Post recorded inputs `vertical_arc_{x,y,oblique}.cl`: the inside ring now runs counter-clockwise. The post's `vertical_arc_entry` checks still hold (G18/G19 arcs, chords for oblique).

## Pins and mutation checks

New pins: `crates/motion/tests/climb_direction.rs` (9 tests), `crates/app/tests/climb_direction.rs` (2 tests, through `operation::generate` with the verify), and `area_open::the_open_pass_runs_climb_with_the_material_on_its_right`. Corrected pins (each still asserts something, none deleted): `contour_inside_shrinks_and_flips_travel` (now CCW), `conventional_inside_travels_reversed` (renamed from `..._forward`; now CW), `machining2d::climb_and_conventional_reverse_the_travel`, `control_comp` / `wear_comp` sides (motion and app; two app fns renamed `..._under_g41_...`). `level_links::contour_ring_to_ring_keep_down_is_proved_or_named` keeps its stay-down cases on conventional and adds the climb case (lifts, named, verify clean). `law_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` (ui) now runs on the conventional walk; see "Not exercised".

What each pin checks, from `climb_direction`:
- Outside contour, climb + M3, runs CW (signed sweep < 0); conventional runs CCW. `climb_outside_contour_runs_clockwise_and_conventional_counter_clockwise`
- Inside contour and round hole wall, climb, run CCW. `climb_inside_contour_...`, `climb_hole_wall_contour_runs_counter_clockwise`
- 2D Pocket wall pass, climb = CCW and conventional = CW, for Waterline, Offset rings, Adaptive and Auto. `pocket_wall_pass_climb_runs_counter_clockwise` (motion), `the_2d_pocket_wall_pass_runs_counter_clockwise_under_climb` (app: block with a 20 x 20 blind hole, Waterline / Offset rings / Adaptive, verify silent, analytic-solid gouge check)
- With control compensation, climb gives G41 and conventional G42, on both sides, and the centre walks the matching direction. `control_compensation_posts_g41_for_climb_and_g42_for_conventional`, plus the posted NC goldens above
- Leads stay on the air side (outside: centre at least 3 mm off the part; inside: within the bore's centre area) and arc leads stay tangent at the join after the flip, for both travels. `leads_stay_on_the_air_side_after_the_flip`, `arc_leads_stay_tangent_after_the_flip`
- Sim / verify: `the_2d_contour_runs_clockwise_outside_and_counter_clockwise_in_the_hole_under_climb` generates outside and hole contours on the block with a hole, with leads None / Arc / Tangential / Perpendicular and both travels. Each gets `operation::generate`'s verify (no warnings) and an analytic-solid gouge scan (no point of the cutter inside the block).
- Chamfer: boss edge CW and bore edge CCW under climb. `chamfer_climb_keeps_the_material_right`

Mutation results. For each, I re-inverted one rule, confirmed red, and restored with `git checkout` (tree clean after):

| Mutation | Red tests |
|---|---|
| M1: ring rule `climb == inside` changed to `!=` | climb_outside..., climb_inside..., climb_hole_wall..., control_compensation..., arc_leads_stay_tangent... |
| M2: `air_side` climb branch put back to air-right | control_compensation..., arc_leads_stay_tangent... |
| M3: `side_of` swapped back (climb = G42) | control_compensation_posts_g41... |
| M4: chamfer rule inverted | chamfer_climb_keeps_the_material_right |
| M5: waterline pocket ring order inverted (shows the pocket pin bites) | pocket_wall_pass_climb_runs_counter_clockwise |
| M6: open-boundary run reversal removed | the_open_pass_runs_climb_with_the_material_on_its_right |
| M7: ring rule inverted, app level | the_2d_contour_runs_clockwise_outside_and_counter_clockwise_in_the_hole_under_climb |
| M8: keep-down link proof without the leads | contour_ring_to_ring_keep_down_is_proved_or_named |

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on 0adc69d3+6a40091e. It fell back to batch size because `cl` was touched. geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion suites passed, and so did `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates. App was red only on `thread_boss` (a stale NC golden, regenerated in 86f73eba, now green). UI was red only on `law_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` (see below; the ui lib is now 731/731 green). The earlier targeted runs of app `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`, `verify`, `operations`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `wall_arc_entry`, `lead_approach`, `arc_entry`, `contour_start_point`, `conformance`, `program_units`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle`, `per_op_files`, `cli`, `corner_blend` and `area_open`, plus the whole post crate, were all green after the golden regeneration.

## Not exercised / follow-ups

- The repro in the issue (the user's end-cap plate over MCP and the Tormach post) was not re-run through the CLI. The same law is pinned through `operation::generate` and the posted NC goldens.
- `ui::law_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` now runs on the conventional walk. At its coarse 0.1 mm tolerance on a tessellated Ø30 cylinder stock, the climb walk's arc fit sits about 0.01 mm past the wall. The verify flags it as a gouge (so the post is held, not silent), and the overlay draws it red instead of green. The arc fitter's split points depend on the walk direction, and this fixture lands on the wrong side of the 0.01 mm gouge tolerance. I'm filing it as a follow-up issue.
- M4 spindle for mill ops: not supported today (only thread milling reverses), so it is not read. The decision file says what has to flip if that ever changes.
- 2D Chamfer `Side::Auto` is treated as a boss edge (material inside the picked loops). A bore edge needs `Side: Inside` to climb counter-clockwise.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: 2D Contour and 2D Chamfer climb milling now runs climb with the M3 spindle - outside profiles clockwise, inside profiles counter-clockwise, G41 under control/wear compensation (BREAKING: posted direction reverses; projects that set climb off as a workaround now post conventional) (#1555)

Fixes #1555

- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_closed.rs` finds the shells the file declares closed (`CLOSED_SHELL`, and the outer shell a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` names) and judges each one's kept mesh (`judge`).
- `step_facets.rs` (new): each tessellation pass keeps every face's mesh apart, oriented as truck's `to_polygon` would, and records the facet range each face owns. `step.rs` uses it in place of `to_polygon`.
- `step_seams.rs` (new): the seams of a closed shell, vertices welded within 1e-6 of the file unit, sorted into three faults:
  - **Reversed face** (a shared edge used twice in the same direction): fixed, not refused. Each face is flipped to agree with its neighbours (exact shared edges, and T-junction sides that run parallel, vote), and each connected group is turned to enclose a positive volume. Logged as a warning naming the face.
  - **T-junction** (neighbouring faces split their shared boundary differently): closed when every boundary edge's ends and midpoint lie within 2 chord tolerances of another face's boundary. Logged.
  - **Gap** (a boundary edge farther than that from every other face): refused. `closed shell #id (N faces) meshes open: K boundary edges lie more than G mm from any other face, most on face #F (i of N), up to W mm; the first from (..) to (..) mm[; face #D got no mesh from the kernel]`.
- A face the kernel returns no mesh for is still refused by name in any shell. Open shells keep the kernel's winding and are not seam-checked.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/1573-closed-shell-watertight.md`, including the Prime-Directive call on the two corpus files (below).

title: fix(bore): refuse a bore too wide for its ring, and keep it out of Detect holes
body:
## What changed

The Bore op's ride is a centre dive, one radial sweep and one ring on the wall. The dive clears radius `r`; the ring clears the band `[rc - r, rc + r]` (`rc = R - r - leave`). They meet only while `rc <= 2r`, so for holes up to **3 x tool diameter + 2 x stock to leave**. Past that, the ride left a core no pass touches. On a through bore it came loose at the last level (the issue's Ø74.3 bore with a 4 mm tool left a Ø66 disc). Generate still said ok, and so did verify.

- **motion** (`machining2d/bore.rs`): a new door refuses such a hole by name at generate. The message gives the hole's diameter and position, the cutter, the ring radius, the core left and the limit, and points the user at a pocket/adaptive op or a larger tool. `max_bore_diameter()` states the limit once.
- **app** (`operation/bore_reach.rs`, `material.rs`): `detect_holes` on a Bore op keeps only the holes its own tool clears and names each one left out (`DetectedHoles { params, skipped }`). If every hole is too wide, the detection is refused and nothing is stored. Drill and Thread ops are not filtered.
- **MCP**: `detect_holes` now answers `skipped` (one sentence per hole left out), and the tool description says so.
- **GUI**: the Detect holes click stores the same `EditOperationParams` through a `DetectedHoles` queue arm, and the status line names the skipped holes. Undo is unchanged.
- The decision is in `docs/decisions/1556-bore-core-door.md`. Refusing was chosen over clearing the floor with more rings (filed as #1566). The limit is 3d from the geometry, not the issue's "about 2d".
- The issue is raised P3 -> P1: a freed core after a clean verify is unsafe output that passes.
- **Review fix (6b327747): the corner radius.** A bull nose or ball on a through hole runs its tip only `THROUGH_CLEAR` (1 mm) under the floor, so at the floor plane it cuts at `(r - cr) + sqrt(a (2 cr - a))`, not `r`. The kernel now carries the tool's `corner_radius` (`BoreParams`) and judges a through hole at that floor reach: the limit is `d + 4 reach + 2 leave` (`3d + 2 leave` for a square end mill or any blind hole). A Ø12 r2 bull nose clears through holes up to 34.928 mm, not 36; between them the old door posted a free C-shaped ridge. The math lives in the new `machining2d::bore_core` (`cutting_radius_at`, `bore_floor_reach`, `bore_core_gap`, `bore_leaves_core`, `max_bore_diameter`), and Detect holes now asks the kernel's own verdict (`bore_leaves_core`) with the same corner and through allowance, so the two agree at the limit and over the leave. A corner that does not fit the cutter is refused by name. Blind holes keep the full radius: the ridge stands on the floor (documented in the decision file, with the derivation).

## How tested

Pins, each mutation-checked:

- `motion` lib `machining2d::bore_core_tests`:
  - `bore_refuses_a_bore_that_would_leave_a_free_core`: Ø74.3 with a 4 mm tool is refused with "74.300 mm hole", "R35.150", "core from 4.000 to 66.300 mm" and "up to 12.000 mm".
  - `bore_refuses_just_past_the_limit_and_takes_the_limit`: a Ø13 hole (4 mm tool, 0.5 leave) bores and its floor is fully covered; Ø13.02 is refused.
  - `every_bore_the_ride_takes_clears_its_whole_floor`: a point-to-chord coverage law at the floor level over five hole/tool ratios.
  - Mutations: removing the door fails both refusal pins. A stricter limit (`rc - r`) fails the limit pin, the coverage law and `bore_rides_the_wall_circle`. A looser one (`rc - 3r`) fails the limit pin.
- `app` `tests/bore_core.rs` (MCP, on a synthetic 200 x 100 x 10 plate with a Ø74.3 through bore beside a Ø6 hole, 4 mm end mill):
  - `detect_holes_leaves_the_wide_bore_out_of_a_bore_op_and_names_it`: 1 hole stored, `skipped` names the Ø74.3, and the Ø6 bore generates and verifies `ok`.
  - `detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_with_only_too_wide_holes_is_refused_by_name`: the refusal stores nothing, and a Drill op on the same plate is not filtered.
  - `a_bore_op_handed_the_wide_bore_by_hand_refuses_at_generate`: a hand-edited list is refused at generate with the numbers, and verify is not ok.
  - Mutations: with no detect filter, all three fail. With no kernel door, the by-hand pin fails and generate answers `ok` (the original bug).
- `ui` lib `detect_holes_note_tests` (GUI parity):
  - `detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_stores_the_small_hole_and_names_the_wide_one`: the status line names the skipped hole.
  - `detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_with_only_a_wide_hole_is_refused`.
  - Mutation: forcing the plain status fails the first.
- Review fix pins (6b327747):
  - `motion` lib `bore_core_tests::the_cutting_radius_follows_the_corner_torus`: flat, bull nose, ball, a ball smaller than the drop, floor reach through vs blind.
  - `bore_core_tests::a_bull_nose_through_hole_is_judged_at_its_floor_reach`: Ø12 r2 through bores at 34.928 with the floor inside the ring's band covered (coverage at the floor-plane reach), refuses 34.948 with the corner's numbers, keeps the 36 mm blind limit, and shows the coverage check sees the 0.27 mm ridge the old limit left.
  - `bore_core_tests::a_ball_through_hole_and_a_corner_that_does_not_fit_are_judged`: Ø6 ball limit 14.944; a 3.5 corner on a 6 mm cutter refused.
  - `app` lib `bore_reach::tests::detect_keeps_the_limit_hole_with_its_leave_and_names_the_one_past_it`: 4 mm tool, 0.5 leave keeps Ø13.000, names Ø13.02.
  - `bore_reach::tests::detect_judges_a_bull_nose_through_hole_at_its_floor_reach`.
  - `app` `tests/bore_core.rs::a_bull_nose_through_bore_is_judged_by_its_corner_at_detect_and_generate` (MCP, a custom Ø12 r2 bull nose): detect skips the Ø35.5 through bore, and generate refuses it handed in by hand with "up to 34.928 mm".
- Fixture changes: three motion fixtures bored Ø20 with a 6 mm tool (3.33 d), a ride that left a ring of floor from Ø6 to Ø8 uncut. They now bore Ø16: the unit test `bore_rides_the_wall_circle`, `tests/center_cut_law.rs::a_tool_that_is_not_centre_cutting_never_plunges_into_a_bore_or_circular` and `tests/level_links.rs::bore_params`. What those tests check is unchanged. No golden and no app fixture held a hole past the limit.
- `tests/thread_boss.rs` reads `.params` from the new return type.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on fce68299: motion 163 s, app 747 s, ui 36 s, 15.8 min wall. An earlier run on e56a4dba failed `center_cut_law` and `level_links`, whose Ø20/6 mm fixtures this law now refuses; they were moved inside the limit.
- Gate on the review fix: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 6b327747: motion 185 s, app 728 s, ui 61 s, 16.3 min wall.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

### Mutation check, review fix (6b327747)

Each mutant run against `motion` lib `bore_core`, `app` lib `bore_reach` and `app` `tests/bore_core.rs`:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| kernel's through reach ignores the corner (full `r`) | killed (5 pins, motion + app) |
| generate passes `corner_radius: 0.0` instead of the tool's `corner_r` | killed (`a_bull_nose_through_bore_is_judged_by_its_corner_at_detect_and_generate`) |
| detect ignores the corner | killed (2) |
| detect ignores `through` (judged as blind) | killed (2) |
| **detect ignores the leave** (the review's survivor) | killed (`detect_keeps_the_limit_hole_with_its_leave_and_names_the_one_past_it`) |
| **detect drops a hole at the limit** (its own strict `dia < max`, the review's `<=` -> `<` survivor) | killed (2) |
| the shared verdict counts touching as a core (`> CORE_TOL` -> `> -CORE_TOL`) | killed (6) |
| torus `sqrt(h (2cr - h))` -> `sqrt(h (cr - h))` | killed (5) |
| corner-fit door removed | killed |
| limit `d + 4 reach` -> `d + 3 reach` | killed (8) |

The review's two survivors no longer exist as written: detect has no comparison of its own, it asks `bore_leaves_core`, the kernel door's verdict.

## Not exercised

- The user's own STEP (`End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step`) is not in the repo. The synthetic plate reproduces the same shape and the same path.
- No pixel snapshots changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill doc (`.claude/skills/`) is a process file and was not touched, so there is no PROCESS_VERSION bump. The tool description in `mcp/tools.rs` carries the `skipped` field.
- An overlap margin at the exact limit (the review's non-blocking note): not taken, touching stays covered; the reason is in the decision file.
- A general "freed piece" law in verify / the stock sim: neither one detects a disconnected piece today. That needs design (some slugs are freed on purpose) and is filed as #1565.

## Follow-ups

- #1565: verify / the stock sim do not detect a freed piece (P8, effort:max).
- #1566: the Bore op could clear wide holes with rings or a spiral instead of refusing them (P7, effort:high).
- #1584: the camcraft-mcp skill row for `detect_holes` should name `skipped` (P5, effort:low; a process file, so not here).
- #1565 carries a note: an old saved project keeps its cached cored path and stamp; a verify-time `bore_leaves_core` check of each Bore op's holes would close it.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` (4364 lines) grew by 26 in this PR; it was far over the 400-line law already. Flagged only.

Changelog: A Bore op refuses, by name, a hole wider than 3 x its tool diameter (+ 2 x stock to leave; less for a bull nose or ball on a through hole, judged at its reach on the floor). Its one ring would leave a free core, which it used to post as ok. Detect holes leaves such holes out of a Bore op and names each one (MCP `skipped`).

title: fix(import): tessellate three-fillet corner blends instead of refusing them
body:
## What changed

A STEP solid whose rounded edges meet in corner blends now imports closed, instead of being refused by #1546's guard (or, before that, hanging: #1536).

The issue assumed truck cannot subdivide the blends because they are not continuous. They are continuous. I rebuilt the #1536 model from the issue's description with solidcore (two L-shaped halves united, all 30 edges rounded R3.125, written by its step-export): 1 shell, 62 faces, 126 edges, 66 vertices, as the issue lists, and the same refusal on d569372f. Two separate faults were measured on it.

**1. The pole (root cause of the hang and of the refusal).** The corner blend is a rational Bezier patch of degree (4, 2) with one side collapsed to the corner vertex. Every parameter along that side is a pre-image of the vertex. truck finds a boundary point's parameters by Newton iteration; at the pole the free parameter came back as **-1,195,342,517** (knot domain 0..1), which truck accepts because the extrapolated rational surface still passes through the vertex. It then subdivides the bounding box of the boundary's parameters: a billion knot spans of extrapolation, which never meets the tolerance. On the knot domain itself the same subdivision ends in 3 to 5 rounds at every tolerance of the schedule.

- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_pole.rs`. The metered surface (`step_guard`) post-processes truck's parameter searches for B-spline and NURBS faces. An answer inside the knot domain is returned untouched. One outside it is replaced by a parameter inside the domain (the previous boundary point's value for each coordinate that left it, else the nearest bound), but only when the surface there is the searched point (truck's own 1e-6). Anything else is left as truck found it, still bounded by #1546's meter.

**2. The edges (a silent wrong mesh behind the refusal).** With the pole fixed alone, the model imported in 2.4 s with no refusal and was wrong: **13,981 mm3 of 19,549.7**, every planar face missing a corner. The rounded edges are `SURFACE_CURVE`s whose master is `.PCURVE_S1.`; truck rebuilds such an edge as a 2D curve on the neighbouring surface, in its own parametrisation of that surface and between parameters it searches for without a hint.

- New `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_edge3d.rs`. Before the shells are converted, every `EDGE_CURVE` on a surface curve is pointed at that curve's `curve_3d`. Switching only the master to `.CURVE_3D.` is not enough: for an edge with `same_sense = .F.` truck 0.3.0 inverts the curve twice on that path (pinned below).

No new tessellator: truck's subdivision is kept, so no other B-spline face changes its mesh. The issue's three options and why they were dropped are in `docs/decisions/1548-bspline-corner-blends.md`.

## Readings

Debug build. "Closed" means 0 unmatched edges.

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| #1536 part rebuilt, 62 faces, on d569372f | refused: "face #14010 (NURBS surface, face 19 of 62 ...) did not converge" |
| same, with this PR | 33,073 facets, closed, **19,545.21 mm3** (stated 19,549.71; the 4.5 mm3 is the inscribed mesh's chord error), 1.3 s |
| same, every edge reversed (`same_sense = .F.`), with this PR | identical: 33,073 facets, closed, 19,545.21 mm3 |
| same, face senses turned, with this PR | 33,236 facets, 19,545.21 mm3. Counted with an earlier rounding-based edge count only: it showed 20 edges, in pairs one rounding step apart (the same point either side of a step). Not re-counted with the welding count the test uses. |
| 30 mm cube, all 12 edges R3.125, on d569372f | imported with no refusal at **14,993 mm3** (57% of the closed form 26,286.4) |
| the same cube written with solidcore's opt-in fixes on, with this PR | 15,820 facets, closed, 26,281.69 mm3. (The cube file of the row above was not re-run after the fix.) |
| `fillet_corner.step` (the fixture), with this PR | imports closed, volume inside the test's bound around the closed form 26,816.49 mm3 |
| the fixture, with this PR but without the pole rule | refused: "face #1228 (NURBS surface, face 2 of 10 ...) did not converge" (mutation 1 below) |

The gate's suites over the existing STEP fixtures are green (below).

## How tested

New fixture `testdata/models/fillet_corner.step` (76 KB): the #1536 part's size, a 30 mm cube centred on the origin, with the three edges at (-15, -15, -15) rounded R3.125. Three cylinders and one corner blend; 12 of its 21 edges are surface curves with a pcurve master. Generated with solidcore (recipe below), face senses turned outward.

Mutation checks: each mutation applied, the test seen RED, then restored and seen GREEN.

| Test | Pins | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `import_step_corner_blend::a_three_fillet_corner_imports_closed_at_its_volume_within_the_chord_tolerance` | default cap, 120 s hard limit; bounds; 0 unmatched edges; volume short of the closed form by 0 ..= 0.005 mm x curved area; `coarse_mm` is `None` | `settle` not applied in the two metered searches | RED: refused, "face #1228 (NURBS surface, face 2 of 10 in shell #1288) ... did not converge within 25000000 evaluations" |
| same | same | `prefer_3d` not called | RED: 24 unmatched edges |
| `import_step_corner_blend::edges_declared_against_their_curves_import_the_same_closed_solid` | every edge rewritten with its vertices swapped and `same_sense = .F.` imports the same solid | edges left on their surface curve (master switched only) | RED: 74 unmatched edges |
| `step_pole::tests::an_outside_answer_that_is_not_a_pole_is_left_as_truck_found_it` | the only guard in the rule: no replacement unless it is the same point | same-point check removed | RED: `(1.0, 0.9)` instead of `(1.0, 2.0)` (also fails `a_non_finite_answer_ends_cleanly`) |
| `step_pole::tests::a_pole_answer_far_outside_takes_the_previous_boundary_points_parameter` | the -1.2e9 reading goes to the previous point's parameter | hint not carried | RED: `(0.0, 0.0)` instead of `(0.0, 1.0)` |
| `step_pole::tests::{an_answer_inside_the_knot_domain_is_returned_untouched, a_pole_answer_with_no_usable_hint_goes_to_the_nearer_domain_bound, a_surface_without_knots_is_never_touched, a_non_finite_answer_ends_cleanly}` | the rest of the rule | - | - |
| `import_step_corner_blend::bent_corner_blends_end_cleanly_and_bounded` | 10 variants of the blend (zero, negative and 1E300 weights; reversed, zero-length, 1E300 and -1E9 knots; the pole pulled apart): each imports finite facets or is refused, inside 90 s | - (degenerate-input pin) | - |

This PR adds no new refusal. Faces that still cannot be subdivided keep #1546's refusal by name (`import_step_guard`, unchanged and green).

Gate on the final head fd1a1c94 (merged with upstream/main f1de41a5):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 56 s. App lib plus bore_facet_sagitta, import_step_corner_blend, import_step_guard, large_models, model_fidelity, step_budget, step_chord_units, step_fidelity, step_nesting, stock_export: 252 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. (The planner mapped the change to these suites; it did not fall back to batch.)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import`: 26 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- **The user's own `sc_logo.step` was not available.** The readings are on a rebuild of that part with solidcore at the pinned rev 55d0e76 with all opt-in fixes on. The topology counts match the issue, but the writer is not the same: the issue's file has 14 spheres and 20 B-spline surfaces, the rebuild 14 rational patches and 6 surfaces of revolution. Please re-run the #1536 repro on a build of this branch; expected is a closed mesh near 19,545 mm3.
- The rebuilt 62-face model and the full rounded cube are not committed (1 MB and 365 KB); only the one-corner fixture is.
- **A closed shell that meshes open is still not refused.** Three bent variants in the fuzz test import with the blend face dropped (138 facets, open). Filed as #1573 (P1).
- Edge-curve and swept-surface divisions and the parameter searches are still unmetered (#1545; one slow reading added there).
- The GUI import path was not run by hand; it calls the same `parse_with_chord_budget`.
- Release-mode timings were not measured.

<details><summary>Fixture recipe (scratch crate, not committed)</summary>

Dependencies: `solidcore` and `step-export` from `https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore` at rev `55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda` (the rev `crates/kernel` pins).

```rust
let mut k = solidcore::Kernel::default();
k.fixes = solidcore::kernel::UpstreamFixes::all();
let mut b = prim::create_box(&mut k, Point3::new(-15.0, -15.0, -15.0), 30.0, 30.0, 30.0)?;
// the three edges with an end at (-15, -15, -15)
let edges: Vec<EdgeId> = /* b.edges() filtered by curve end points */;
fillet_edges(&mut k, &mut b, &edges, 3.125, 1, 1, 1.0)?;
let text = step_export::write(&step_export::brep_to_model(&b)?)?;
```

Then every `ADVANCED_FACE` sense and every `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` orientation is flipped (the writer's senses came out inward), and `FILE_DESCRIPTION` is replaced. The 62-face model is the same with four boxes united into the two L halves and all 30 edges rounded.
</details>

title: fix(circular): judge a whole-model Circular against the finished part
body:
## What changed

A Circular whose source is the finished part (a whole model, `SrcRef::Entity` with `part_solid` true) is now judged against that part. `depth_law_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`) gave every Circular `DepthLaw::None`, so a circle typed through the part's wall generated with no warning on the operation. It now takes `DepthLaw::Section` (the section and solid laws Contour, Face and the picked pockets answer to) through one shared function:

```rust
pub(super) fn authored_law(src: &SrcRef) -> DepthLaw  // Entity -> Section; Stock, Selection -> None
```

It is written for every kind that cuts geometry typed by hand (Circular's centre and radius here; the Slot's endpoints and width in #1537, where SKULL can call it; coordination comment on #1537). It runs after `depth_law_of`'s `part_solid` early return, so a Stock source (or an entity that is the setup's stock) still cuts unjudged. A picked Circular keeps its law (`None`).

**Root cause / readings.** The old contract said "the source is the material to remove, not a part to keep", which holds only for a Stock source. On main, in the readings taken (radius-12 circle in a radius-10 through hole, 6 mm end mill, 0.5 left), the operation carried **0 warnings** (status ok, no MCP `verify` finding on the op). The post was held only by the program-level stock sim (`post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 719 cell(s), worst 8.00 mm`). Now the operation itself carries blocking `Warning::Gouge`s on the moves that enter the wall (1028 over MCP), `held_by: ["C1"]`.
