title: fix(fixtures): a flipped setup's fixtures are judged against the carried stock's shape, not its box
body:
Branched from upstream main.

## What changed

The check for fixtures in a carried setup (`app::fixture_carried`) used to judge each fixture by its world bounding box. A vise's box spans the opening between its jaws. A soft-jaw nest pocket sits inside the jaws' box. So a part clamped between the jaws, or seated in the nest, was reported as "standing inside the stock carried from Setup 1", and the post was refused (#1530: 4.48 mm and 11.43 mm deep).

- **Box first, then mesh.** The box is still the first check. When it flags a fixture, the fixture's closed world mesh is then read column by column against the carried stock. For each column it takes the Z spans the mesh puts on the column's vertical line and compares them with the column's material.
  - The line reading is the new `FixtureMesh::steel_on_line` in `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/column.rs`.
  - It uses signed crossings with the same nonzero/odd-parity rule as the existing point-in-solid test.
  - Touching or overlapping shells merge into one span.
  - An ambiguous line (one through a facet edge, or one lying in a wall face) is nudged by one millionth of the mesh's scale, capped at 0.1 micron a step, and read again.
  - A line whose winding goes negative or does not close at zero (an inside-out shell over another) is not read: the box stands.
- **Between the columns, read whole (review rework).** Every rectangle spanned by four neighbouring material columns, trimmed by the contact tolerance, is judged against the material the four share by the new `FixtureMesh::steel_in_prism` (`crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/prism.rs`). Facets clipped to the rectangle that reach into the material slab convict. With no facet over the rectangle, there is no steel there. Otherwise the slab holds no surface, and one line decides whether it is all steel or all air. Nothing inside the material is sampled, so a post or a lip narrower than the pitch is refused. Where the four columns disagree (a side face or a step runs through), only what they share is judged: a boundary is known to one pitch, as with the box law.
- **Contact tolerance.** A column is refused only when the overlap is more than `CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL` (0.01 mm). That must hold on the centre line and on four lines 0.01 mm beside it, so a face that lies exactly on a column centre counts as contact.
- **The mesh can only clear a fixture, never add a hit.** In these cases the box depth stands, as before:
  - an open or refused mesh;
  - a coarse-fidelity fixture (#864);
  - a line that no nudge can read, or that winds inconsistently;
  - a rectangle between the columns that cannot be read;
  - a spent facet-visit budget (`MESH_VISIT_BUDGET`, 50 M visits per fixture, logged when it runs out);
  - a footprint narrower than one grid cell.
- **Bounded time.** A column or rectangle whose box depth cannot exceed the worst depth already found is skipped. A fixture that really penetrates therefore stops after its first refused column.
- **Refusal text.** A fixture that really enters the carried material is still refused by name with its depth, in the same message as before.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1530-carried-fixture-shape.md`.

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/carried_fixture_shape.rs`:
- **Setup.** A 50 x 50 x 10 part in 56 x 56 stock. Setup 1 contours its sides down to Z 4, leaving a 3 mm brim (the hat). Setup 2 flips it over X (AlignPartToSetup FlipX) and faces the brim side. In Setup 2 the section stands at Z 0..6 and the brim at Z 6..10.
- **Pins.** Each also checks that the post gate reports the same lines:
  - `the_flipped_hat_enters_setup2_section_down_brim_up`: the fixture geometry is real, and the grid pitch is under 0.5 mm.
  - `a_builtin_vise_gripping_the_flipped_parts_sides_is_held`: built-in 5 in vise, jaws 5 mm high, faces at Y ±25, floor at Z 0. Accepted.
  - `a_vise_jaw_moved_into_the_part_is_refused_by_name_with_its_depth`: opening 48. Refused, `5.00 mm deep`.
  - `soft_jaws_whose_nest_clears_the_part_are_held`: one-piece soft jaws (5 shells) whose pocket clears the part by 0.05 mm. Accepted.
  - `soft_jaws_with_a_nest_too_small_are_refused_by_name_with_the_depth`: pocket 0.5 mm too small on each side. Refused, `fixture 'Soft jaws' ... setup 'Setup1' ... 5.00 mm deep`.
  - `a_nest_floor_a_hair_past_the_contact_tolerance_is_refused`: nest floor 0.03 mm into the part, 0.02 mm past the tolerance. Refused, `0.03 mm deep`.
  - `a_nest_floor_touching_within_the_contact_tolerance_is_held`: floor 0.005 mm into the part. Accepted.
  - `a_post_narrower_than_the_pitch_between_the_columns_is_refused`: the review's 0.19 x 0.19 post, 3 mm in, on no column line. Refused, `3.00 mm deep`.
  - `a_lip_narrower_than_the_pitch_between_the_columns_is_refused`: the review's 0.19 x 48 lip, 4 mm in. Refused, `4.00 mm deep`.
  - `an_open_mesh_keeps_the_box_verdict`: the clear nest with one facet removed. Refused, `5.00 mm deep` (box).
  - `a_coarse_fidelity_fixture_keeps_the_box_verdict`: the clear nest flagged coarse (#864). Refused, `5.00 mm deep` (box).

New `crates/app/tests/carried_fixture_guards.rs` calls `mesh_penetration` on hand-built carried bodies, so each guard is reached on its own:
- `an_unread_column_line_keeps_the_box_depth` (budget 0 gives the box depth)
- `an_inside_out_shell_between_the_columns_keeps_the_box_depth`
- `a_post_between_the_column_lines_is_steel`
- `a_fixture_narrower_than_a_cell_off_the_lines_keeps_the_box_depth`
- `a_face_on_a_column_centre_where_the_material_ends_is_contact`
- `a_rectangle_reads_its_contact_band_at_the_tolerance` (second review): a block mid-cell, 0.03 mm into the material, refused `Some(0.03)`; 0.005 mm, `None`.
- `a_rectangle_is_trimmed_by_the_tolerance_only` (second review): a 0.015 mm post at x 1.512..1.527 (past the line at 1.51), refused `Some(3.0)`.
- `a_pitch_too_fine_to_trim_keeps_the_box_between_the_columns` (second review): at a 0.015 mm pitch, a 0.003 mm post 3 mm in mid-cell is refused at 3.0, as the box refuses it.

Second review, also in `carried_fixture_shape.rs`: `a_turned_setup_judges_its_fixture_in_the_turned_frame`, a 60 x 30 bar with Setup2 turned 90 degrees about Z (not flipped). A pocket fitting the turned brim is held; 1 mm short it is refused `4.00 mm deep`; the same pocket read in the unturned frame would be refused 10 mm deep (checked by hand).

**Slim rectangles (second review).** Below a 0.02 mm pitch the rectangle trimmed by the tolerance inverts. It is now tested as slim before the off-footprint `continue` (which an inverted rectangle always took, clearing it), so it is unread and keeps the box depth. The line and prism readings' other early-outs were re-read: a facet index the mesh does not hold now reads unread (both), and a non-finite clip reads as steel over the slab, so neither can clear.

New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_column.rs` tests `steel_on_line` directly:
- block span / miss
- a line on a facet diagonal is nudged and read
- nest pocket vs wall, with touching shells merged
- a line in a wall face is still read
- a spent budget reads nothing
- non-finite input is not read
- an inside-out shell over another is not read as air (the review's A 0..10 / B 5..15 reversed)
- a 6 micron block at X 5000 is read where it stands (capped nudge)
- a budget cut mid-line never reads part of a line
- `steel_in_prism`: a post no line meets is steel; a box wholly inside steel is steel; contact band; budget, NaN and inverted input are unread

The existing `carried_fixtures_cache.rs` passes unchanged, including the sub-cell dowel-pin pin.

### Mutation checks
The full table (the review's M1-M10 plus the rework's guards) is in the PR comment for head 87f657fa; the second review's P2b, P2c and P5 are now red (PR comment for head a4befa9b). Every guard is red under its mutation except two: M5 (centre line only) is stricter, not looser, and G2 (the winding must close at zero) is a defensive guard that only a partial reading reaches, and the budget guard pinned by M4 already catches that.

### Performance (release, M-series Mac, re-measured after the second review)
- Pins: `carried_fixture_shape` 0.59 s debug for all 12. `carried_fixture_guards` under 0.01 s.
- 400 k-facet fixtures: a 100 k-segment cylinder whose cap fans every line and rectangle near the centre meets, plus a tall block so the box flags every column (radius 3-9.5 mm, pitch 0.2-1.0 mm).
  - With no limit: up to 13.8 s (449 M visits).
  - With the 50 M-visit budget the time is the budget times the cost of a visit: 0.33 s when the visits are line reads, 1.6-2.2 s when they are rectangle clips (the worst seen). M3 measured 0.74-0.80 s on its construction. A spent budget keeps the box verdict, logged.

## Gates
On head a4befa9b (merges cleanly with upstream main):
- App, all green: lib 194; carried_fixture_shape 12; carried_fixture_guards 8; carried_fixtures_cache 7; accessory_collisions 2; builtin_vise 9; fixture_* (keys_lenient, law_gaps, library, locate, locate_stock, mesh, mesh_posed, plate, plate_detect, plate_followups, plate_riders, route, ux); fixtures 14; posting 17; setup_carry 9; verify 21; verify_arc_reading 7.
- Sim, all green: lib 146; fixture_mesh_column 12; fixture_mesh_convict 5; fixture_mesh_posed 9 (1 ignored); posed_band_cylinder 3.
- Sim also: fixture_mesh 9 (1 ignored), fixture_arc_sagitta 10, fixture_stack_span 8, posed_fixture 7, posed_fixture_midpose 3, c_axis_fixture 8.
- Clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-app --all-targets` clean. `-p camcraft-sim` lib and fixture_mesh_column clean. The sim `--all-targets` run stops on a lint already on main in `fixture_mesh_convict.rs`, a file this PR does not touch.

## Not exercised
- The MCP `add_builtin_vise` replay of the user's h5 project; the pins rebuild the same geometry headlessly.
- A real STEP soft-jaw import.
- Inside the material nothing is sampled. At a side face or a step, contact is resolved to the carried grid's pitch, as with the box law: steel at most one pitch into the material at the face, short of the next column centre, can pass. The M3 review found the side verdicts equal to main's at every phase and ruled it non-blocking; it is stated in the decision record and filed as #1580 (P7).
- A strip 0.02 mm wide (2 x the contact tolerance) along each column line is read only by the five lines: a wall thinner than that lying on a line passes. This is the contact tolerance by design and is stated in the decision record.
- Seen while building the pins and not followed up: in 60 x 60 stock, a 15.24 mm contour around a 50 x 50 part left the stock's outer corners (about 1.5 mm triangles) at full height in the carried body. The pins use 56 x 56 stock. This may need its own issue.

Changelog: A flipped (carried) setup's fixtures are judged by their real shape against the stock carried from the earlier setup, so a vise gripping the part's sides or soft jaws with a nest are no longer refused; steel truly inside the carried part is still refused with its depth.

In the browser (wasm) build the File commands did nothing: every picker went through `file_dialog.rs`, whose wasm half answers "cancelled" and only logs why. Now:

- **Save, Save As and Post download.** The app layer gains `project::save_text` and `posting::post_setup_unwritten` - the same collect, the same gate and engine run, bytes held in memory. The desktop's `save` / `post_setup` now call them and write the result, so the two cannot drift. The UI hands the bytes to the browser (`crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs`: `Blob` + `URL.createObjectURL` + a hidden `a[download]` click, through `eframe::web_sys`; no new dependency). Save As asks for the name with `window.prompt`. A downloaded document is marked clean; the unsaved prompt's Save downloads too. A refused post offers nothing and opens the refusal window, as on the desktop.
- **Everything else is refused by name and visibly disabled.** `browser_files::refusal` is the one table: opening anything (model, project, fixture, machine, post, theme, tool library, tool body) needs the browser file picker (#31, PR #1314); recent files, the fixture library folder and the per-operation folder post cannot exist in a page; setup sheet / tool list / stock STL / tool library exports are not downloads yet (#1437). `State::run` refuses those on the status line before anything else; ribbon cells (Model, Project, Post when per-op) are darkened with the reason as their tip; page buttons are greyed with the reason as their hover text. Context-menu rows and the theme dropdown's Browse row refuse on the status line only.
- `State::browser_build` (set from `cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32")`) carries the law, so the native tests drive it.

Inventory of every dialog call site and what the browser did: issue comment on #1431. Decisions: `docs/decisions/1431-wasm-file-commands.md`.

**Not stacked on PR #1314** (a contributor's fork branch). The open paths stay owed to it; when it lands, its commands come off `browser_files::refusal`. Hence `Refs #1431`, not `Fixes`.

- `crates/app/tests/unwritten_post.rs`: `the_unwritten_post_is_the_written_program_byte_for_byte`, `the_unwritten_post_refuses_where_the_written_one_does`, `save_text_is_the_saved_project_file` - 3 passed.

#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203.

**GUI hand check needed.** The handles, the drag feel and the readout were tested only through the kittest harness and headless state tests. Nobody has looked at them on screen yet.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A seventh bar button (a four-armed cross) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default, it is view state like pick-through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the part's bounding-box centre and each ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at any zoom. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** Pressing a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. Empty space still orbits. While the button is down, the preview slides the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows just above the bar. The distance is where the cursor ray comes closest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the Model page's own `MoveModel::new`, with the rotation copied bit for bit. That means one undo step, the same staleness, the same following stock and the same fixture-clash warning as a typed move. No new placement path.
- **What adds no history step:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends where it began, and turning Move off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag happens in that setup's frame. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis the user sees.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/1198-drag-to-move.md`: only parts are dragged in this slice, Move mode is off by default, and the preview moves the body only.

## MCP
No new app command, so no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`, and the MCP `move_model` tool already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make every move a drag makes.

## How tested
- `egui_app::tests::body_drag` (kittest, the real shell; 5 tests):
  - `handles_show_only_in_move_mode_on_a_selected_part`: a ball per axis, constant size when zoomed out, gone when Move is off.
  - `a_ball_drag_is_one_undoable_move_by_the_dragged_distance`: the preview never writes the world; the release moves the part by the dragged distance along X only; one undo returns the history to clean.
  - `escape_mid_drag_cancels_with_no_history_step`
  - `a_drag_that_ends_where_it_began_adds_nothing`: also checks that a press on a ball is not a pick.
  - `empty_space_still_orbits_in_move_mode`
- `move_drag_tests` (headless state; 5 tests):
  - `the_drag_distance_is_the_axis_point_under_the_cursor`: 12.5 mm along Y; one queued command.
  - `a_press_off_the_balls_is_not_a_drag`
  - `a_turned_setup_moves_the_part_along_the_axis_it_shows`
  - `the_rotation_is_kept_bit_for_bit`
  - `a_non_finite_distance_is_refused_by_name`
- The existing bar laws hold with the seventh button: `viewport_bar::tests::bar_fits_its_buttons` and `law_tests::view_cube_tests::the_hud_is_laid_out_from_the_pane_alone`, which iterates every button in `NAVS`.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): ui lib plus the boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell and theme_files suites. 752 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

- **`crates/ui/src/file_pick.rs`** (new): the browser picker. On wasm32, `open()` makes an `<input type=file>` whose `accept` comes from the dialog's filters, clicks it and returns at once. When the user has chosen, the file's name and bytes go into a thread-local inbox, and the next frame is woken through the egui context, which `shell_web` registers.
  - Files over 256 MiB (`BROWSER_READ_LIMIT`) are refused by name before they are read. A failed allocation in wasm aborts the tab.
  - The input and its change closure are held in one slot until the next pick, not `forget`ed, so a cancelled picker does not leak.
  - The inbox, `accept_attr` and `too_big` are plain Rust on every target.
- **`crates/ui/src/state_picked.rs`** (new):
  - `open_model_dialog` / `open_project_dialog`: rfd's synchronous dialog on native (unchanged), the async picker on wasm32.
  - Each frame, `drain_actions` turns every inbox entry into a `CommandKind::OpenPicked`. A model goes through `ImportModel::from_bytes` and `finish_import`: one undo step, and a same-named model is an update. A project goes through `project::open_noted`.
  - A failed read, a refused import, or a project that is not text or not JSON is said on the status line ("import refused: …" / "open failed: …") and changes nothing.
- **`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`**: `ImportModel::from_bytes(file_name, data, budget)`. It shares the path import's laws through `checked_budget`: IGES and unknown extensions refused, the STEP budget's bounds. It adds the `MAX_FILE_BYTES` cap and the finite-mesh gate. `geometry::import::parse_model_graded_within` is now `pub`.
- **`crates/ui/src/state.rs`**:
  - Two new `CommandKind` arms route to the functions above.
  - The model and project dialogs' filters are factored out (`mesh_dialog`, `project_dialog`) so both pickers ask with the same ones.
  - `open_project_path`'s reset is factored out as `reset_for_open`, so the bytes open retires the old document the same way. Behaviour is unchanged.
- No dependency added. The picker uses `eframe::web_sys` features that eframe already enables (`HtmlInputElement`, `File`, `FileList`, `Blob`).
- **Safari fix (after the user's hand check, 2026-11-13).** `State::run_click_actions` runs the queue at the end of the clicked frame when it holds an action that may open a chooser (Open model, Open project, the unsaved-changes answer). eframe runs that frame inside its `pointerup` listener, so `input.click()` now happens inside the user's click; before, the queue ran at the start of the next frame, from requestAnimationFrame, where Safari ignores it without a word. The hidden input is now attached to the page with `display:none` and removed when replaced. A chooser asked for from the Cmd/Ctrl+O shortcut (a later frame) says on the status line to click File > Model / File > Open if no chooser appeared.
- The browser build no longer starts with "no theme folder found beside the exe" (`theme_dir::startup_status`).
- **Merge with #1431 (main):** main refused Open model / Open project in the browser until this picker landed; `browser_files::refusal` no longer refuses them, `NEEDS_PICKER` now names the pickers still owed, and the #1431 tests assert the two cells live.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/31-wasm-file-picker.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests:
  - `crates/app/tests/import_bytes.rs`:
    - `picked_bytes_import_like_the_same_file_from_disk`: the same name, mesh and fidelity as the disk import, for STL, OBJ and STEP.
    - `picked_bytes_are_refused_by_name_never_a_panic`: IGES, an unknown extension, no extension, empty or corrupt files of each format, and a budget given for a non-STEP file.
  - `crates/ui/src/file_pick_tests.rs`:
    - `a_picked_model_imports_through_the_undoable_command`
    - `a_picked_file_that_cannot_be_used_is_refused_by_name`
    - `a_picked_project_opens_in_place_of_the_document`
    - `the_browser_picker_accepts_the_dialogs_extensions`
    - `a_file_over_the_browser_read_limit_is_refused_before_it_is_read`
    - `a_chooser_asked_for_by_a_click_opens_inside_that_click` (Safari fix)
    - `a_chooser_outside_a_click_says_what_to_do_instead_of_failing_silently` (Safari fix)
  - `theme_dir::tests::the_browser_build_never_says_a_theme_folder_is_missing_beside_an_exe`
  - `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `egui_app::tests::browser_files::{the_ribbon_keeps_open_live_in_the_browser, a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored}` (merge with #1431)
- **Safari fix push (head 0dd7eebc, merges upstream/main f84059c9):** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (app suites 69 s, ui suites 67 s); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` built with no camcraft warnings (stock macOS bash now runs it) and `web/check-app-page.sh target/web` passed. A plain `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` is not possible here: flecs' C needs the script's wasi sysroot.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. The app suites (lib, import_bytes, large_models, model_fidelity, step_*, stock_export, bore_facet_sagitta) passed in 21 s. The ui suites (lib, boundary, boundary_picks, feedback, fixtures, gpu_render, machine, models, operations, shell, theme_files) passed in 19 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (native, macOS).
- **wasm check**: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` passed on macOS, using the official rustc 1.99.1 with the wasm32 std and Homebrew LLVM's clang for the wasi C.
  - It linked `camcraft-cli.wasm` and `camcraft_ui.wasm`, ran wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and laid out `target/web`. The shim answers all nine WASI imports.
  - camcraft-ui raised no warnings.

The input was clicked from the next egui frame (requestAnimationFrame), outside the click; Safari ignores it there. It is now clicked at the end of the clicked frame, which eframe runs inside its `pointerup` listener (see the PR comment for the sources). title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.
- `motion` unit test `the_cone_rule_holds_the_lean_and_refuses_a_lead_into_a_corner`; `post` unit test `taper_angle_words_parse_and_garbled_ones_refuse_the_file`.
- U/V goldens: `wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_verify` pass with their goldens unedited.
- Merge-time refresh (merge of upstream main df90b031, head 9673a77e): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 21.1 min; 3215 tests passed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; golden `wire_taper_angle_punch.nc` unchanged.
- Gate on the pre-refresh head 39d014d8: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/537-wire-4axis` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 11.2 min); the wire suites by hand (wire_taper 5, wire_4axis 6, wire_post 5, wire_contour 7, wire_verify 3, wire_taper_angle 4: all pass); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10). The angle code and dialect words are invented on the synthetic fixture.
- How a real control ramps the lean over the lead-in and lead-out is modelled as a linear ramp, the same as #536. The decision record states this.
- The `arc` corner rule (lean change rounded over a stated radius) is not offered.
- No UI page field for `edm.taper_angle`. It is machine-file data only, like `edm.codes`.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a machine can state an angle-word taper dialect (edm.taper_angle: side rule and mitre/cone corner rule). The wire post writes the angle word, and the verify judges the lean the stated corner rule cuts.

### Review fixes at b1c287a0 (the mutation check on 9673a77e)
Tests only, plus one behaviour-neutral extraction: the angle-word lean in `posting_wire::stream` moved into `angle_lean()` so its three door-shadowed refusals can be unit-tested. No golden or snapshot changed. Each line below was deleted (or neutralised) and its test went RED, then went GREEN again once the line was restored.

| Line (review) | Mutation | Killing test |
|---|---|---|
| `operation/wire_op.rs:176-177` stamp of `taper_angle` | both `h.write` lines dropped | `wire_taper_angle::the_corner_rule_and_the_dialect_each_move_the_stamp` (mitre != cone, U/V != mitre, U/V != cone) |
| `wire-iso.cps:205` `angle4` | refuse line deleted | `script_wire_iso::an_angle_word_section_posts_and_each_missing_piece_is_refused_by_name` (zero taper; WireFourAxis) |
| `wire-iso.cps:210` `acode` | refuse line deleted | same test (no `edm.codes.taper_angle`) |
| `wire-iso.cps:216` `angtpl` | refuse line deleted | same test (template without `{angle}`) |
| `wire-iso.cps:305` `ang` | refuse line deleted | same test (`WireAngle` with no dialect) |
| `posting_wire.rs:166` 4-axis refusal (now in `angle_lean`) | `if false && four` | `posting::wire::tests::an_angle_lean_refuses_a_four_axis_cut_an_unstated_rule_and_an_unresolved_top` |
| `posting_wire.rs:170` `complete()` | rules defaulted | same test |
| `posting_wire.rs:171` top unresolved | `top.unwrap_or(0.0)` | same test |
| `posting_wire.rs:326` lean changes side | `return Err` deleted | `posting::wire::tests::a_lean_that_changes_side_or_never_leans_is_refused_by_name` |
| `posting_wire.rs:333` no leaning side | `sign.unwrap_or(1.0)` | same test |
| `edm_taper.rs:89` not an object | `if false && !v.is_object()` | `machine::edm_taper::tests::a_taper_angle_not_an_object_or_a_garbled_side_refuses_the_file` |
| `edm_taper.rs:103` `positive` garble | `.unwrap_or(AngleSide::TopLeft)` | same test |
| `edm.rs:81` `"taper_angle"` in `WIRE_KEYS` | key dropped (array of 5) | `machine::edm::tests::a_sinker_stating_taper_angle_is_refused_as_a_wire_key` |
| `motion/src/wire_edm/taper.rs:222` cone turn-back | `if false && phi.abs() > ...` | `wire_edm::taper::tests::the_cone_rule_refuses_a_ring_that_turns_back_on_itself` |

Why 166/170/171 are pinned and not removed: generation's door (`wire_op::corner_rule`) and the stamp keep these cases out of a real post today. They stay as the post's own guard, so a 4-axis path never posts with angle words if it reaches the post some other way. `angle_lean` makes that guard testable.

title: feat(edm): Wire Contour skim passes - per-pass condition, offset and direction
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551). fork synced at v0.19.0.

Expected merges: retarget to `main` after #1139 merges. #1143 (Wire UI, also on #1139) touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs`; this PR changes one line there (the op destructure gains `..`), so a trivial conflict at most. #534 (verify) and #1109 (open profile) on #1123 are not touched.

## What changed

The Wire Contour gains skim passes: a rough pass, then N skims, each naming its own machine condition (and so its own offset, wire radius + that condition's gap), with an optional direction reversal per skim.

- `operation::WireContourOp.skims: Vec<WireSkim { condition, reverse }>`; file / MCP JSON `skims: [{ condition, reverse? }]`, absent when empty (rough-only files and goldens unchanged). Edits ride `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the existing MCP params door.
- Command door (`wire_op::condition_of`): every skim's condition resolved through #531's door, refused by name when it names none or the machine does not state it; then `motion::wire_edm::check_passes`: a pass nearer the profile than the finishing (last) pass ("would cut past the finished profile", rough included), a skim farther out than the pass before it ("would cut only air"), a skim condition with another wire diameter ("one threading cuts every pass with one wire").
- Generator: `motion::wire_edm::wire_passes` (new `skims.rs`) runs #532's single-pass generator per pass at its own offset, every law at that offset; each pass leads in from the threading point and back; a reversed skim walks clockwise. No skims is `wire_contour` exactly.
- Stamp digests each skim's condition numbers and direction (writes nothing for no skims - no stored stamp moves).
- Post stream (`posting_wire`): a mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition <skim id>` before each skim's first move (after each return to the threading point); a path that does not return once per pass is refused.
- `wire-iso.cps`: a condition that arrives with the wire threaded is the next skim's - `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `comp_off` again at its first move; the wire stays threaded.
- **Wire laws (#534) and skims** (merge with main, 2026-11-13): `sim::verify::wire` now judges each move at its own pass's kerf. Before this, every move was judged at the rough's kerf, which read skim 1 as a false 0.0200 mm gouge at move 8 (0.165 - 0.145). `WireJob.skim_offsets`, new `passes.rs`: the path is split at each return to the threading point, the threading law takes the widest pass, and the slug law sweeps each pass at its own offset. Skims on an open run are refused at the door and in the law. The arithmetic is in the decision record.
- **Sodick wire post refuses skims** (second merge-time refresh, main after #1506): `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` writes its C condition word once, at threading, so a skim's mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition` would only have reassigned a variable and every skim would have been cut on the rough pass's condition. A condition change after the section's first cut is now refused by name: "Sodick: a condition change between passes (skims) is not supported by this post - post the skims through wire-iso or as separate operations". No C word is written per pass (no public Sodick source for a mid-program condition change, #617). `wire-iso.cps` is the only other shipped wire post and already selects per pass, so it is unchanged. Main's `sodick_wire_post.rs` literal gains `skims`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

## How tested

- New golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` (rough C110 + skim S21 + reversed skim S31 on #533's synthetic fixture): three distinct offsets (X-20.165 / -20.145 / -20.135), three condition selects, one thread, one cut.
- `wire_post`: `a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`, `no_skims_is_the_rough_program_and_json_unchanged`, `skims_edit_undo_and_round_trip`, `each_skim_refusal_is_named_at_the_door`; the existing `the_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate` passes with #533's golden unchanged (no golden moved).
- `camcraft-motion` unit: `skims_cut_their_own_offsets_and_none_is_the_single_pass`, `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`.
- `camcraft-sim` unit: `verify::wire::tests::each_pass_is_judged_at_its_own_kerf`, `passes_that_cannot_be_told_apart_are_unreadable`.
- `wire_contour` suite (all 7) green; `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head 0e96ca1c: motion, app (every suite - the new golden is shared input) and ui suites, 0 failed (12.4 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- `sodick_wire_post::skims_are_refused_by_name_never_cut_on_the_rough_condition`: a rough C110 + skims C121, C131 through `post_script` is refused by name with no file, and through the engine neither skim C word is written. **Mutation check:** with the refusal block removed from `sodick-wire.cps` the test is RED (the skimmed program posted, `expect_err` panicked); restored, GREEN. Sodick goldens and `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` unchanged.
- Second refresh, head 7d8a125a: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` post, sim, motion, app, ui suites 0 failed (31.8 min), the four pinning tests included; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-{geometry,cl,tools,post,sim,motion,app,ui} --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the fixture's conditions and codes are synthetic (three synthetic conditions S21, S31, W20 added to it).
- A punch drops after its rough unless held - tabs are #539; the program does not claim a hold.
- No UI editor for the skim list yet: follow-up #1148 (after #535 / #1143).

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: Wire Contour skim passes - a rough pass then N skims, each at its own machine condition's offset (optionally reversed), posted by the generic ISO wire post with a condition select per pass; out-of-order or unstated skims refused by name (#538)

Fixes #538

title: feat(ui,mcp): work offsets listed by the setup's post; MCP takes an index (#931 slice 3)
body:
## #931 slice 3 of 3: the Setups combo lists the post's offsets; MCP takes an index

**Stacked on #1113 → #1101** (#945, the former bottom of the stack, merged 2026-11-12). This PR targets `main`, so until those merge its diff also shows their commits. This slice is its own `feat(ui,mcp): ...` and `fix(ui): ...` commits. Merge order: #1101, #1113, then this one. Fork synced at v0.19.0.

**Process change: yes** (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, the `set_work_offset` row). By the current process rule this PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` (it carries main's); the merging session handles the number and the #681 note.

Effort: high (no escalation).

### What changed
- **Setups page / WCS page combo** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_pick.rs`): lists offsets `1..=max` of the setup's **own** post (`setup::work_offset_names`, the cached table from slice 2). Each entry reads "Work offset n (NAME)", or "Work offset n" when the post gives that offset no name. The default post shows 6 entries. Tormach PathPilot shows 9 (G59.1-G59.3). If a setup holds a pick its post cannot express, for example offset 9 after switching to a six-offset post, that pick still shows as itself: "Work offset 9 - not on this post", listed alone after 1-6. It is never shown as offset 1. The post gate from slice 2 refuses it by setup name.
- **The wording is one function in app**: `setup_offsets::entry_label`.
- **Other UI words.** Slice 2 already moved the browser tree, the heights row, the viewport chips and the status line to the app's names. This slice changes the three texts that still named a fixed "G54-G59" range: the combo's hover, the heights page hint, and the WCS page's "Work offset:" line. The WCS page line appears in a release-lane snapshot, which gets regenerated at the cut; its structural twin `one_wcs` is updated here. I left the probe page's "Set G54".."Set G59" alone on purpose: the probe register arithmetic only reaches offsets 1-6 (triage point 4).
- **MCP `set_work_offset`** (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`):
  - It takes `index`, 1-based. The words `G54`-`G59` are accepted as aliases of 1-6.
  - `word` stays as the older spelling of the same argument. If both are given they must agree.
  - `setup_offsets::parse_index` checks only the shape and the 1-255 sanity bound. The post's range is checked by `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` → `setup_offsets::check`, so the refusal is the same one the GUI gives, by setup name.
  - Replies carry `index`, `name` and `word` (an alias of `name`). So do `set_wcs` and `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs` (`mcp/job.rs`).
- **camcraft-mcp skill doc**: documents the new `set_work_offset` arguments and replies.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-ui.md`.

### How it was tested
- New: `crates/app/tests/mcp_work_offset.rs` (4 tests):
  - `set_work_offset_takes_a_one_based_index_and_answers_index_name_and_word`
  - `the_legacy_words_are_aliases_of_offsets_one_to_six`
  - `an_offset_the_setups_post_cannot_express_is_refused_by_setup_name`

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

**R comes from the rounded words' own ladder (M3 review fix, head 0bb37ddd).** The control reads the posted words, each rounded to the least increment on its own. In inch, `Q157 P472 R0.0157` left k − d = 0.0315 one increment past the second rung 0.0314, so the control cut a 4th, unverified pass. Now the post counts the record's rough passes N from its own ladder, rebuilds rungs N−1 and N from the rounded Q (first depth), Q (minimum depth) and P (thread height), and writes the R whose last rough depth P − R lies in (rung N−1, rung N], nearest the record's allowance. Inch golden: `R0.0157` → `R0.0158` (control: 0.0157 / 0.0314 / 0.0472). If that R is more than one least increment from the record's allowance, the cycle is refused by name (the Q/Q/P words and the R window are named). The other G76 words (X, Z, P k, Q dd, Q dmin) are each one record value rounded once, not differences, so R was the only derived word. The Tormach (LinuxCNC) G76 has the same class of gap in J/K (inch `J0.0314 K0.0944` = ceil 4 passes for a 3-pass record), filed as #1619. Its goldens are left byte-identical to main here.

**A project cached before this fix posts R0 until the op is regenerated.** Checked: the stale stamp (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`, `current_stamp`) hashes only the operation's inputs (tool, params, source, heights). It has no generator version, and the cached record's `finish_allowance` reads back as saved. So such an op reads **Fresh**, not Stale, and posts the old `R0` schedule (one extra root pass, mm) until it is regenerated. The stale-stamp machinery does not catch it today.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- M3 review fix (head 0bb37ddd), two new tests in `lathe_post_g76_schedule`:
  - `the_default_thread_g76_states_its_three_passes_in_inch`: posts the default thread under G20, parses the G76 words, runs the control's ladder on them, and asserts exactly 3 passes matching the laid depths (`R0.0158`).

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
**Stacked on #437** (#418), which is on #433 (#417) and #432 (#416). Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the #419 work is 68bd14a5. Part of #363.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Fixes #419
